title.raw: 卷一百三十三 列傳第七十一: 叛臣 張覺子:僅言 耶律餘睹 窩斡 Volume 133 Biographies 71: Pan Chen, Zhang Jue son: Jinyan, Ye Luyudu, Wo Wo

sentences.zh: 古書「畔」與「叛」通，畔之為言界也。

translations.literal: In ancient books the character pan meaning 'border' and pan meaning 'rebel' are interchangeable; pan in the border sense means a boundary.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient texts the characters pan meaning 'border' and pan meaning 'rebel' were used interchangeably, because pan in the border sense denotes a boundary.

sentences.zh: 《左氏》曰，政猶「農之有畔」，是也。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says, governing is like "a farmer having boundaries" — that is the point.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary observes that governing a state is like a farmer keeping to his furrows — and so it is.

sentences.zh: 君臣上下之定分，猶此疆彼界之截然，違此向彼，即為叛矣。

translations.literal: The fixed roles of ruler and minister, superior and inferior, are like the sharp division between this territory and that; to turn from the one toward the other is rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The settled order between ruler and subject, superior and inferior, is as clear-cut as one border against another; to abandon this side for that is to rebel.

sentences.zh: 善惡判于跬步，禍患極於懷襄，吁，可畏哉！

translations.literal: Good and evil are decided within a few steps; disaster reaches to the floods of Huai and Xiang — ah, how fearsome!
translations.idiomatic: Right and wrong may turn on a single step, and calamity may swell to the scale of the Huai and Xiang deluges — how dreadful!

sentences.zh: 作《叛臣傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore the "Biographies of Rebel Ministers" was composed.
translations.idiomatic: Hence this "Biographies of Rebel Ministers."

sentences.zh: 張覺，亦書作鐧，平州義豐人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jue, also written as Zhang Jian, was a native of Yifeng in Ping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jue — the name is also written Zhang Jian — came from Yifeng in Ping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在遼第進士，仕至遼興軍節度副使。

translations.literal: He placed as a jinshi in the Liao examinations and rose to vice military commissioner of Liaoxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He had passed the Liao jinshi examination and served as vice military commissioner of the Liaoxing Army circuit.

sentences.zh: 太祖定燕京，時立愛以平州降，當時宋人以海上之盟求燕京及西京地，太祖以燕京、涿、易、檀、順、景、薊與之。

translations.literal: When the Taizu Emperor secured Yanjing, Shi Li'ai surrendered Ping Prefecture; at that time the Song, invoking the maritime alliance, sought Yanjing and the Western Capital territories, and the Taizu Emperor gave them Yanjing together with Zhuo, Yi, Tan, Shun, Jing, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taizu Emperor took Yanjing, Shi Li'ai surrendered Ping Prefecture. The Song, citing the maritime alliance, demanded Yanjing and the Western Capital lands; the Taizu Emperor yielded Yanjing along with Zhuo, Yi, Tan, Shun, Jing, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 平州自入契丹別為一軍，故弗與，而以平州為南京，覺為留守。

translations.literal: Ping Prefecture, since entering Khitan control, had formed a separate army district, so it was not given away; instead Ping was made the Southern Capital and Jue was appointed as its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Prefecture had become a separate military district under the Khitan and was therefore withheld; it was made the Southern Capital instead, with Jue as military governor.

sentences.zh: 既而聞覺有異志，上遣使劉彥宗及斜缽諭之，詔曰：「平山一郡今為南京，節度使今為留守。

translations.literal: Soon word came that Jue harbored disloyal intentions; the emperor sent Liu Yanzong and Xiebo to instruct him, with an edict saying: "The single commandery of Pingshan is now the Southern Capital; the military commissioner is now the military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When reports reached the court that Jue was disloyal, the emperor dispatched Liu Yanzong and Xiebo to admonish him. The edict read: "The Pingshan region is now the Southern Capital, and your former title of military commissioner is now military governor.

sentences.zh: 恩亦厚矣。

translations.literal: Our favor has also been generous.
translations.idiomatic: Our favor toward you has been ample.

sentences.zh: 或言汝等陰有異圖，何為當此農時輒相扇動，非去危就安之計也。

translations.literal: Some say you secretly harbor other designs — why, at this season of farming, do you stir people up? That is not a plan for leaving danger and seeking safety.
translations.idiomatic: Some claim you are plotting in secret. Why stir unrest in the middle of the planting season? That is no way to trade peril for security.

sentences.zh: 其諭朕意。

translations.literal: Convey my meaning to them.
translations.idiomatic: Make our intent known to them."

sentences.zh: 」太祖每收城邑，往往徙其民以實京師，民心多不安，故時立愛因降表曾言及之。

translations.literal: "Whenever the Taizu Emperor took a city, he often moved its people to fill the capital, and popular hearts were largely uneasy; therefore Shi Li'ai had once mentioned this in his surrender memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Taizu Emperor captured a city he tended to relocate its population to bolster the capital, which unsettled the people — a grievance Shi Li'ai had raised in his surrender memorial.

sentences.zh: 及以燕京與宋而遷其人，獨以空城與之，遷者道出平州，故覺因之以作亂。

translations.literal: When Yanjing was given to the Song and its people were relocated, only an empty city was handed over; the evacuees passed through Ping Prefecture, so Jue took advantage of this to raise rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanjing was ceded to the Song its inhabitants were uprooted, leaving an empty city behind. The displaced traveled through Ping Prefecture, and Jue seized the moment to rebel.

sentences.zh: 天輔七年五月，左企弓、虞仲文、曹勇義、康公弼赴廣甯，過平州，覺使人殺之于栗林下，遂據南京叛入于宋，宋人納之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year of Tianfu, Zuo Qigong, Yu Zhongwen, Cao Yongyi, and Kang Gongbi were traveling to Guangning and passed through Ping Prefecture; Jue had men kill them under the chestnut grove, then seized the Southern Capital and rebelled by submitting to the Song, who accepted him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianfu 7 (1123), Zuo Qigong, Yu Zhongwen, Cao Yongyi, and Kang Gongbi were bound for Guangning and passed through Ping. Jue had them ambushed in the chestnut grove, seized the Southern Capital, and defected to the Song, who welcomed him.

sentences.zh: 太祖下詔諭南京官吏，詔曰：「朕初駐蹕燕京，嘉爾吏民率先降附，故升府治以為南京，減徭役，薄賦稅，恩亦至矣，何苦輒為叛逆？

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor issued an edict to instruct the officials of the Southern Capital, saying: "When I first halted my chariot at Yanjing, I praised you officials and people for being the first to submit; therefore I raised your prefecture to the Southern Capital, reduced corvée labor, and lightened taxes — our favor has been complete. Why must you rashly rebel?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu Emperor addressed the Southern Capital officials: "When I first encamped at Yanjing I commended you for leading the surrender, elevated your prefecture to the Southern Capital, eased corvée burdens, and lightened taxes. Our kindness has been full. Why court rebellion?

sentences.zh: 今欲進兵攻取，時方農月，不忍以一惡人而害及眾庶。

translations.literal: Now I wish to advance troops to attack and seize it, but it is the farming season; I cannot bear to harm the multitude because of one wicked man.
translations.idiomatic: I am ready to march and take the city, yet it is planting season and I will not let one villain bring ruin on the common people.

sentences.zh: 且遼國舉為我有，孤城自守，終欲何為？

translations.literal: Moreover the entire Liao state has become mine; to hold a lone city by yourselves — what can you ultimately hope for?
translations.idiomatic: The Liao realm is already mine. What end can a lone stronghold serve?

sentences.zh: 今止坐首惡，餘並釋之。」

translations.literal: Now only the chief culprit will be punished; all the rest will be released."
translations.idiomatic: Only the ringleader will be punished; the rest shall go free."

sentences.zh: 覺兵五萬屯潤州近郊，欲脅遷、來、潤、隰四州。

translations.literal: Jue's army of fifty thousand encamped in the suburbs of Run Prefecture, intending to coerce the four prefectures of Qian, Lai, Run, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Jue massed fifty thousand troops near Run Prefecture, aiming to intimidate Qian, Lai, Run, and Xi into submission.

sentences.zh: 闍母自錦州往討之，已敗覺兵，欲乘勝攻南京，時暑雨不可進，退屯於海堧。

translations.literal: Zhamu marched from Jin Prefecture to attack him, already having defeated Jue's troops and wishing to press the advantage against the Southern Capital; at that time summer rains made advance impossible, so he withdrew and encamped at the sea embankment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhamu marched from Jin Prefecture, routed Jue's force, and prepared to storm the Southern Capital, but summer rains stalled the advance and he fell back to camp on the coastal levee.

sentences.zh: 無何，闍母再敗覺兵，復與戰於兔耳山，闍母大敗，覺報捷于宋。

translations.literal: Before long Zhamu again defeated Jue's troops, then fought again at Rabbit-Ear Mountain; Zhamu suffered a great defeat, and Jue reported victory to the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhamu beat Jue again, but at Rabbit-Ear Mountain Zhamu was routed in turn. Jue sent word of victory to the Song court.

sentences.zh: 宋建平州為泰寧軍，以覺為節度使，張敦固等皆加徽猶閣待制，以銀絹數萬犒軍。

translations.literal: The Song established Ping Prefecture as the Taiping Army circuit, appointed Jue as military commissioner, promoted Zhang Dun'gu and others to Huayou Pavilion academicians, and rewarded the army with tens of thousands in silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Song reorganized Ping as the Taiping Army circuit, named Jue its military commissioner, promoted Zhang Dun'gu and others to Huayou Pavilion academicians, and sent tens of thousands in silver and silk to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 宗望軍至南京城東，覺兵大敗宵遁，遂奔宋，入於燕京。

translations.literal: Zongwang's army reached the east of the Southern Capital city; Jue's troops were greatly defeated and fled by night, then ran to the Song and entered Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang's army reached the eastern approaches of the Southern Capital, Jue's force was shattered and fled under cover of night. He escaped to the Song and took refuge in Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 宗望以納叛責宋宣撫司，索張覺。

translations.literal: Zongwang charged the Song Pacification Commission with harboring a rebel and demanded Zhang Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang accused the Song Pacification Commission of sheltering a rebel and demanded Zhang Jue's surrender.

sentences.zh: 宣撫王安中匿之於甲仗庫，紿曰：「無之。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Wang Anzhong hid him in the armory and deceived them, saying: "He is not here.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Wang Anzhong hid him in the armory and lied, "He is not here.

sentences.zh: 」宗望索愈急，安中乃斬貌類覺者一人當之，金人識之曰：「非覺也。

translations.literal: "Zongwang's demands grew more urgent; Anzhong then beheaded one man who resembled Jue to pass off as him, but the Jurchens recognized him and said: "This is not Jue.
translations.idiomatic: "As Zongwang pressed harder, Anzhong executed a look-alike and presented the head. The Jurchens recognized the deception: "That is not Jue.

sentences.zh: 」安中不得已，引覺出。

translations.literal: "Anzhong had no choice but to bring Jue out.
translations.idiomatic: "Forced to comply, Anzhong produced Jue.

sentences.zh: 數以罪，覺罵宋人不容口，遂殺覺函其首以與金人。

translations.literal: He enumerated his crimes; Jue cursed the Song without pause, so they killed Jue, boxed his head, and gave it to the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: After listing his crimes, Jue poured unceasing abuse on the Song. They executed him, packed his head in a box, and handed it to the Jurchens.

sentences.zh: 燕京降將及常勝軍皆泣下，郭藥師自言曰：「若來索藥師當奈何？

translations.literal: The surrendered generals of Yanjing and the Ever-Victorious Army all wept; Guo Yaoshi said to himself: "If they come to demand Yaoshi, what then?
translations.idiomatic: Yanjing's surrendered commanders and the Ever-Victorious Army wept openly. Guo Yaoshi muttered, "If they come for me next, what then?

sentences.zh: 」自是，降將卒皆解體。

translations.literal: "From this time the surrendered generals and soldiers all lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: "From that day the morale of every surrendered officer and soldier collapsed.

sentences.zh: 及金人伐宋，竟以納平州之叛為執言雲。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens later attacked the Song, they ultimately took sheltering the Ping Prefecture rebel as their stated cause.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens later invaded the Song, they cited the sheltering of the Ping Prefecture rebel as their justification.

sentences.zh: 子僅言。

translations.literal: His son Jinyan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jinyan.

sentences.zh: 子 僅言

translations.literal: Son: Jinyan
translations.idiomatic: Son: Jinyan

sentences.zh: 僅言幼名元奴。

translations.literal: Jinyan's childhood name was Yuannu.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyan's childhood name was Yuannu.

sentences.zh: 宗望攻下平山，僅言在繈褓間，裏人劉承宣得之，養於家。

translations.literal: When Zongwang captured Pingshan, Jinyan was still in swaddling clothes; a fellow townsman, Liu Chengxuan, obtained him and raised him in his home.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang took Pingshan, Jinyan was still an infant. A neighbor, Liu Chengxuan, took him in and raised him.

sentences.zh: 其鄰韓夫人甚愛之。

translations.literal: A neighbor, Lady Han, loved him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor, Lady Han, doted on the boy.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，因隨韓夫人得見貞懿皇后。

translations.literal: When he was several years old, he followed Lady Han and was able to meet Empress Zhenyi.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of a few years he accompanied Lady Han to an audience with Empress Zhenyi.

sentences.zh: 留之籓邸，稍長，侍世宗讀書，遂使僅言主家事，繩檢部曲，一府憚之。

translations.literal: She kept him at the princely residence; when he grew somewhat older he attended the Shizong Emperor in his studies, and then had Jinyan manage household affairs, tightening discipline over the retainers — the whole mansion feared him.
translations.idiomatic: She kept him at the princely residence. As he grew he attended Prince Shizong's studies, then put Jinyan in charge of the household, tightening discipline over the retainers until the entire mansion stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 僅言能心計，世宗倚任之，凡宮室營造、府庫出納、行幸頓舍皆委之。

translations.literal: Jinyan was skilled in calculation; the Shizong Emperor relied on him, entrusting to him all palace construction, treasury receipts and disbursements, and arrangements for imperial journeys and halts.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyan had a keen head for accounts, and the Shizong Emperor relied on him for palace construction, treasury affairs, and every detail of imperial travel and lodging.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗曰：「一經僅言，無不愜朕意者。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor once said: "Once it passes through Jinyan, nothing fails to satisfy my intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizong Emperor once remarked, "Whatever passes through Jinyan's hands suits me perfectly.

sentences.zh: 」六年，提舉修內役事，役夫掘地得白金匿之，事覺，法當死，僅言責取其物與官，釋其罪。

translations.literal: "In the sixth year he was put in charge of inner-palace repair labor; laborers digging earth found hidden white metal and concealed it. When the matter came to light the law called for death, but Jinyan compelled them to surrender the goods to the state and released them from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: "In year 6 he oversaw inner-palace repairs. Laborers unearthed hidden silver and kept it secret. When the case surfaced the statute demanded death, but Jinyan made them turn the metal over to the treasury and spared their lives.

sentences.zh: 尋兼祗應司。

translations.literal: Soon he also held the Attendance Office concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given concurrent charge of the Attendance Office.

sentences.zh: 遷少府監，提控宮籍監、祗應司如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of the Palace Workshops, continuing to supervise the Palace Registry Office and the Attendance Office as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director of the Palace Workshops while retaining supervision of the Palace Registry and Attendance offices.

sentences.zh: 護作太甯宮，引宮左流泉溉田，歲獲稻萬斛。

translations.literal: He oversaw construction of the Taining Palace, drew the palace's leftward flowing spring to irrigate fields, and harvested ten thousand bushels of rice each year.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising construction of Taining Palace, he channeled a spring west of the palace to irrigate fields that yielded ten thousand bushels of rice a year.

sentences.zh: 十七年，複提點內藏，典領昭德皇后山陵，遷勸農使，領諸職如故。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he again supervised the inner treasury, directed Empress Zhaode's mausoleum works, was promoted to Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, and retained all his previous posts.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he again oversaw the inner treasury, directed Empress Zhaode's tomb works, was promoted to Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, and kept his other posts.

sentences.zh: 僅言雖舊臣，出入左右，然世宗終不假以權任。

translations.literal: Although Jinyan was an old retainer who attended him at left and right, the Shizong Emperor never entrusted him with real power.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jinyan was a longtime companion who attended him constantly, the Shizong Emperor never gave him substantive authority.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，尚書省奏，宮苑司直長黎倫在職十六年，請與遷敘。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Secretariat memorialized that Li Lun, chief clerk of the Palace Parks Office, had served sixteen years and requested promotion in rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year 21 the Secretariat reported that Li Lun, chief clerk of the Palace Parks Office, had served sixteen years and sought a promotion.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此朕之家臣，質直人也，今已老矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This is my household retainer, a plain and honest man, and he is old now.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He is a household retainer of mine, plain and honest, and he is old now.

sentences.zh: 如勸農使張僅言亦朕舊臣，純實頗解事，凡朝廷議論，內外除授，未嘗得干預。

translations.literal: Like the Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture Zhang Jinyan, also an old retainer of mine — sincere and quite capable — yet in all court deliberations and appointments within and without, he has never been allowed to intervene.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture Zhang Jinyan is another old retainer — sincere and capable — yet he has never been permitted to meddle in court debates or civil and military appointments.

sentences.zh: 朕觀自古人君為讒諂蒙蔽者多矣，朕雖不及古人，然近習憸言未嘗入耳。

translations.literal: I observe that from antiquity many rulers have been blinded by slander and flattery; I may not equal the ancients, yet the crafty words of close attendants have never entered my ears.
translations.idiomatic: I see that many rulers of old were blinded by flatterers and slanderers. I may not match the ancients, but the honeyed words of favorites have never reached my ears.

sentences.zh: 」宰臣曰：「誠如聖訓，此國家之福也。

translations.literal: "The chief ministers said: "Truly as Your sagely instruction states — this is the fortune of the state.
translations.idiomatic: "The chief ministers replied, "Your words are true — this is the state's good fortune.

sentences.zh: 」世宗欲以為橫海軍節度使，而不可去左右，遂止。

translations.literal: "The Shizong Emperor wished to make him military commissioner of the Henghai Army, but could not bear to have him leave his side, and so desisted.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor considered appointing him military commissioner of the Henghai Army but could not part with his constant presence and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 僅言始得疾，猶扶杖視事，疾亟，詔太醫診視，近侍問訊相屬。

translations.literal: When Jinyan first fell ill he still leaned on his staff to attend to duties; when the illness grew critical an edict ordered imperial physicians to examine him, and close attendants came one after another to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinyan first fell ill he still leaned on his staff to work. As the sickness worsened the emperor ordered imperial physicians to attend him, and close attendants came in steady succession to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 及卒，上深惜之，遣官致祭，賻銀五百兩、重彩十端、絹二百匹，棺槨、衣衾、銀汞、斂物、葬地皆官給，贈輔國上將軍。

translations.literal: When he died the emperor deeply mourned him, sent officials to perform sacrifices, granted five hundred taels of silver, ten bolts of heavy-colored silk, and two hundred bolts of plain silk as funeral gifts, and provided coffin, burial garments, silver funerary goods, encoffining items, and burial ground from the state, posthumously enfeoffing him as Supporter-of-the-State Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the emperor grieved deeply, dispatched officials to offer sacrifices, and granted five hundred taels of silver, ten bolts of fine silk, and two hundred bolts of plain silk. Coffin, shroud, silver grave goods, encoffining supplies, and burial ground were all provided by the state, and he was posthumously enfeoffed Supporter-of-the-State Grand General.

sentences.zh: 耶律余睹

translations.literal: Yelü Yudu
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Yudu

sentences.zh: 太祖已取臨潢府，賜詔余睹曰：「汝將兵在東路，前後戰未嘗不敗。

translations.literal: After the Taizu Emperor had taken Linhuang Prefecture, he granted an edict to Yudu saying: "You command troops on the eastern route; in battle after battle you have never failed to be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taizu Emperor captured Linhuang, he sent Yudu an edict: "You command the eastern route, and battle after battle you have never won.

sentences.zh: 今聞汝收合散亡，以拒我師。

translations.literal: Now I hear you are gathering the scattered and lost to resist my army.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear you are rallying the scattered remnants to resist my armies.

sentences.zh: 朕已於今月十五日克上京，今將往取遼主矣。

translations.literal: I have on the fifteenth of this month already taken the Upper Capital; now I am going to seize the Liao ruler.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth of this month I took the Upper Capital, and I am now marching to capture the Liao emperor.

sentences.zh: 汝若治兵一決勝負，可指地期日相報。

translations.literal: If you wish to array your troops and settle victory or defeat in one contest, you may designate a place and date and inform me.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to muster your forces and settle matters in a single battle, name the place and day and send word.

sentences.zh: 若知不敵，當率眾來降，無貽後悔。

translations.literal: If you know you cannot prevail, you should lead your multitude to surrender and not leave yourself regret.
translations.idiomatic: If you know you cannot prevail, lead your men in surrender before regret overtakes you.

sentences.zh: 」及太祖班師，闍母等還至遼河，方渡，余睹來襲，完顏背答、烏塔等殿，力戰卻之，獲甲馬五百匹。

translations.literal: "When the Taizu Emperor withdrew the army, Zhamu and others returned to the Liao River and were in mid-crossing when Yudu came to attack; Wanyan Beida, Wuta, and others served as rearguard, fought fiercely and repelled him, and captured five hundred sets of armor and horses.
translations.idiomatic: "When the Taizu Emperor withdrew, Zhamu and the others recrossed the Liao River. Midway across, Yudu struck. Wanyan Beida, Wuta, and others held the rear, fought him off, and seized five hundred sets of armor and mounts.

sentences.zh: 天輔五年，余睹送款于咸州路都統，以所部來降，乞援接于桑林渡。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu, Yudu sent his pledge of submission to the Xianzhou Circuit commander-in-chief, came to surrender with his following, and requested escort at Sanglin Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 5 Yudu submitted his allegiance to the Xianzhou circuit commander, came over with his command, and asked to be received at Sanglin Ford.

sentences.zh: 都統司以聞，詔曰：「余睹到日，使與其官屬偕來，餘眾處之便地。

translations.literal: The commander's office reported upward; an edict said: "On the day Yudu arrives, have him come together with his officials; settle the rest of his followers in a suitable place.
translations.idiomatic: The commander's office reported to court. The edict read: "When Yudu arrives, let him come with his officers; settle the rest of his followers where convenient.

sentences.zh: 」無何，余睹送上所受遼國宣誥，及器甲旗幟等，與將吏韓福奴、阿八、謝老、太師奴、蕭慶、醜和尚、高佛留、蒲答、謝家奴、五哥等來降。

translations.literal: "Before long Yudu presented the Liao state commissions and patents he had received, together with weapons, armor, banners, and standards, and came to surrender with his officers Han Funu, Aba, Xie Lao, Taishinu, Xiao Qing, Chouheshang, Gao Foliu, Puda, Xiejianu, Wuge, and others.
translations.idiomatic: "Shortly afterward Yudu presented the Liao commissions and patents in his possession, along with arms, armor, banners, and standards, and surrendered with his officers Han Funu, Aba, Xie Lao, Taishinu, Xiao Qing, Chouheshang, Gao Foliu, Puda, Xiejianu, Wuge, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 余睹作書，具言所以降之意，大概以謂：「遼主沉湎荒于遊畋，不恤政事，好佞人，遠忠直，淫刑吝賞，政煩賦重，民不聊生。

translations.literal: Yudu wrote a letter fully explaining his reasons for surrendering, in general stating: "The Liao ruler is sunk in dissipation and wastes himself on hunting, does not care for government affairs, favors flatterers and keeps the loyal and upright at a distance, imposes excessive punishments and is stingy with rewards, government is burdensome and taxes heavy, and the people cannot make a living.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu wrote at length explaining why he had surrendered. In essence he said: "The Liao ruler is sunk in pleasure and idle hunting, neglects government, favors flatterers and keeps loyal men at bay, imposes cruel punishments yet is stingy with rewards, and burdens the people with heavy taxes until they cannot survive.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「樞密使得裏底本無材能，但阿諛取容，其子磨哥任以軍事。

translations.literal: "He also said: "The Bureau of Military Affairs chief Delidi has no talent whatsoever but only flatters to win favor; his son Moge is entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: "He added that Bureau chief Delidi had no ability and survived only by flattery, while his son Moge had been put in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「文妃長子晉王素系人望，宜為儲副，得裏底以元妃諸子己所自出，使晉王出繼文妃。

translations.literal: "He also said: "The eldest son of Consort Wen, the Prince of Jin, has long commanded popular regard and ought to be heir apparent; Delidi, because the sons of the Primary Consort were his own offspring, had the Prince of Jin adopted out to Consort Wen.
translations.idiomatic: "He said the Prince of Jin, eldest son of Consort Wen, enjoyed wide esteem and should have been heir, but Delidi — whose own sons were born to the Primary Consort — had the prince adopted to Consort Wen instead.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「晉王與駙馬乙信謀複其樞密使，來告余睹共定大計，而所圖不成。

translations.literal: "He also said: "The Prince of Jin and the imperial son-in-law Yixin plotted to restore his post as Bureau chief and came to inform Yudu to settle a great plan together, but what they schemed did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: "He reported that the Prince of Jin and imperial son-in-law Yixin had plotted to restore the prince's bureau post, sought Yudu's help to carry out a larger design, and failed.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「己粗更軍事，進策遼主，得裏底蔽之，遼主亦不省察。

translations.literal: "He also said: "I myself had roughly reorganized military affairs and presented strategies to the Liao ruler, but Delidi concealed them and the Liao ruler likewise did not examine the matter.
translations.idiomatic: "He said he had reorganized military affairs and offered counsel to the Liao emperor, but Delidi suppressed it and the emperor never looked into the matter.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「大金疆土日辟，余睹灼知天命，遂自去年春與耶律慎思等定議，約以今夏來降。

translations.literal: "He also said: "The Great Jin's territory expands day by day; Yudu clearly perceives Heaven's mandate, and therefore from last spring onward he fixed plans with Yelü Shensi and others, agreeing to surrender this summer.
translations.idiomatic: "He declared that as the Jin realm expanded daily he saw Heaven's mandate clearly, and from the previous spring had agreed with Yelü Shensi and others to surrender that summer.

sentences.zh: 近聞得裏底、高十捏等欲發，倉卒之際不及收合四遠，但率傍近部族戶三千、車五千兩、畜產數萬、遼北軍都統以兵追襲，遂棄輜重，轉戰至此。

translations.literal: Recently hearing that Delidi, Gao Shinie, and others were about to move, in the urgency of the moment he could not gather the distant quarters in time, but led only the nearby tribal households — three thousand families, five thousand carts, and tens of thousands of livestock; the Northern Liao army commander pursued with troops, so he abandoned baggage and fought his way here.
translations.idiomatic: Learning recently that Delidi and Gao Shinie were about to strike, he had no time to rally distant tribes and led only three thousand nearby households, five thousand carts, and vast herds. The Northern Liao army commander pursued, forcing him to abandon his baggage train and fight his way here.

sentences.zh: 所有官事職位姓名、人戶畜產之數，遣韓福奴具錄以聞。

translations.literal: As for all official posts, names, numbers of households and livestock, he sent Han Funu to record them fully and report.
translations.idiomatic: Han Funu was dispatched to record and report every office, name, household, and head of livestock in detail.

sentences.zh: 」遂與其將吏來見，上撫慰之，遂賜坐，班同宰相，賜宴盡醉而罷。

translations.literal: "Thereupon he came to audience with his officers; the emperor comforted him, granted him a seat, ranked him with the chief ministers, and gave a banquet until all were drunk before dismissing them.
translations.idiomatic: "He then came to audience with his officers. The emperor received him kindly, seated him in the rank of chief ministers, and feasted the company until all were drunk.

sentences.zh: 上命余睹以舊官領所部。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Yudu to lead his following under his former title.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Yudu to command his following under his former title.

sentences.zh: 且諭之曰：「若能為國立功，別當獎用。

translations.literal: He also instructed him: "If you can render merit for the state, you will separately be rewarded and employed.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Serve the state well and further rewards will follow.

sentences.zh: 」自余睹降，益知遼人虛實矣。

translations.literal: "From the time of Yudu's surrender, the court came to know ever more clearly the true condition of the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: "After Yudu's surrender the court understood the Liao's true weakness all the more clearly.

sentences.zh: 余睹在軍中屢乞侍妾及子，太祖疑之，詔咸州路都統司曰：「余睹家屬，善監護之。

translations.literal: While in the army Yudu repeatedly begged for concubines and his son; the Taizu Emperor grew suspicious and edicted the Xianzhou Circuit commander's office: "Yudu's family members — guard them well.
translations.idiomatic: In camp Yudu repeatedly asked for concubines and his son. The Taizu Emperor grew suspicious and ordered the Xianzhou commander's office, "Guard Yudu's family closely.

sentences.zh: 」複詔曰：「余睹降時，其民多強率而來者，恐在邊生變，宜徙之內地。

translations.literal: "Another edict said: "When Yudu surrendered, many of his people were forcibly led along; fearing trouble on the frontier, they should be moved inland.
translations.idiomatic: "A second edict warned, "Many of his people followed under coercion when he surrendered. Move them inland lest they stir trouble on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 」都統杲取中京，余睹為鄉導，與希尹等招撫奚部。

translations.literal: "Commander Gao took the Central Capital; Yudu served as local guide and, together with Xiyin and others, pacified the Xi tribes.
translations.idiomatic: "When Commander Gao took the Central Capital, Yudu guided the advance and, with Xiyin and others, pacified the Xi tribes.

sentences.zh: 奉聖州降，其官吏皆遁去，余睹舉前監酒李師夔為節度使，進士沈璋為副使，州吏裴賾為觀察判官。

translations.literal: When Fengsheng Prefecture surrendered its officials all fled; Yudu recommended the former wine supervisor Li Shikui as military commissioner, jinshi degree-holder Shen Zhang as vice commissioner, and prefectural clerk Pei Ze as administrative judge.
translations.idiomatic: When Fengsheng Prefecture surrendered its officials fled. Yudu nominated the former wine supervisor Li Shikui as military commissioner, jinshi Shen Zhang as vice commissioner, and prefectural clerk Pei Ze as administrative judge.

sentences.zh: 沈璋招集居民還業者三千餘，遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: Shen Zhang gathered more than three thousand residents who returned to their occupations, and was transferred to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Zhang brought back more than three thousand residents to their livelihoods and was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 久之，耶律麻者告余睹、吳十、劉剌結黨謀叛，及其未發宜先收捕。

translations.literal: After a long while Yelü Mazhe reported that Yudu, Wu Shi, and Liu La had formed a faction plotting rebellion, and that before they acted they should be seized first.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Yelü Mazhe reported that Yudu, Wu Shi, and Liu La were plotting rebellion together and should be arrested before they acted.

sentences.zh: 上召余睹等從容謂之曰：「今聞汝謀叛，誠然邪，其各無隱。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Yudu and the others and said calmly: "I now hear you are plotting rebellion — is it true? Each of you, hide nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Yudu and the others and said calmly, "I hear you are plotting rebellion. Is it so? Speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 若果去，必須鞍馬甲胄器械之屬，當悉付汝，吾不食言。

translations.literal: If you truly wish to leave, you will need saddles, horses, armor, weapons, and the like — I shall give them all to you; I do not break my word.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly mean to go, you will need horses, armor, and arms — I will furnish them all. I do not break my word.

sentences.zh: 若再被擒，無祈免死。

translations.literal: If you are captured again, do not pray for exemption from death.
translations.idiomatic: If you are captured again, do not expect mercy.

sentences.zh: 欲留事我，則無懷異志，吾不汝疑。

translations.literal: If you wish to remain and serve me, then harbor no other intent — I will not suspect you.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to stay and serve me, harbor no second thoughts and I will not doubt you.

sentences.zh: 」余睹等戰慄不能對，乃杖鐸剌七十，餘皆不問。

translations.literal: "Yudu and the others trembled and could not answer; thereupon Duo La was beaten seventy strokes, and the rest were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: "Yudu and the others trembled and could not speak. Duo La alone was beaten seventy strokes; the rest went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 天會三年，大舉伐宋，余睹為元帥右都監，宋兵四萬救太原，余睹、屋里海逆擊於汾河北，擒其帥郝仲連、張關索，統制馬忠，殺萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhui a great campaign was launched against the Song; Yudu served as right overseer of the grand marshal. Song troops forty thousand strong came to relieve Taiyuan; Yudu and Wulihai counterattacked north of the Fen River, captured their commanders Hao Zhonglian and Zhang Guansuo and the controller Ma Zhong, and killed more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 3 the Jin launched a major invasion of the Song. Yudu served as right overseer under the grand marshal. Forty thousand Song troops marched to relieve Taiyuan; Yudu and Wulihai met them north of the Fen River, captured commanders Hao Zhonglian and Zhang Guansuo and controller Ma Zhong, and killed more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 宗翰伐宋，余睹留西京。

translations.literal: When Zonghan attacked the Song, Yudu remained at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Zonghan invaded the Song, Yudu stayed behind at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 天會十年，余睹謀反，雲內節度使耶律奴哥等告之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianhui Yudu plotted rebellion; the Yunnei military commissioner Yelü Nuge and others reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 10 Yudu plotted rebellion. Yunnei military commissioner Yelü Nuge and others exposed the plot.

sentences.zh: 余睹亡去，其黨燕京統軍蕭高六伏誅，蔚州節度使蕭特謀自殺。

translations.literal: Yudu fled; his faction's Yanjing army commander Xiao Gao Liu was executed, and Weizhou military commissioner Xiao Te attempted suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu fled. His confederate Yanjing army commander Xiao Gao Liu was executed, and Weizhou military commissioner Xiao Te tried to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 邊部斬余睹及其諸子，函其首以獻。

translations.literal: Frontier units beheaded Yudu and his sons, boxed their heads, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier forces hunted down Yudu and his sons, boxed their heads, and sent them to court.

sentences.zh: 耶律奴哥加守太保兼侍中，趙公鑒、劉儒信、劉君輔等並授遙鎮節度使以賞之。

translations.literal: Yelü Nuge was promoted to acting Grand Guardian and concurrent Palace Secretariat director; Zhao Gongjian, Liu Ruxin, Liu Junfu, and others were all appointed distant-prefecture military commissioners as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Nuge was promoted to acting Grand Guardian and concurrent Palace Secretariat director. Zhao Gongjian, Liu Ruxin, Liu Junfu, and others received distant military commissions as rewards.

sentences.zh: 移剌窩斡，西北路契丹部族。

translations.literal: Yila Wo Wo, of the Khitan tribal groups of the Northwestern Route.
translations.idiomatic: Yila Wo Wo belonged to the Khitan tribes of the Northwestern Route.

sentences.zh: 先從撒八為亂，受其偽署，後殺撒八，遂有其眾。

translations.literal: He first followed Saba in rebellion, accepted a false appointment from him, later killed Saba, and thereby came to possess his following.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed Saba's rebellion, accepted a post in Saba's regime, then killed Saba and took over his followers.

sentences.zh: 撒八者，初為招討司譯史。

translations.literal: Saba had at first been a translator-clerk in the Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Saba had begun as a translator-clerk in the Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 正隆五年，海陵征諸道兵伐宋，使牌印燥合、楊葛盡征西北路契丹丁壯，契丹人曰：「西北路接近鄰國，世世征伐，相為仇怨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenglong the Hailing Emperor levied troops from all circuits to attack the Song, sending Paoyin Zaohe and Yang Ge to conscript all able Khitan men of the Northwestern Route; the Khitan people said: "The Northwestern Route lies close to neighboring states; generation after generation we have campaigned against one another and become mutual enemies.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 5 the Hailing Emperor mobilized troops from every circuit for the Song campaign and sent Paoyin Zaohe and Yang Ge to draft every able Khitan man on the Northwestern Route. The Khitan protested: "Our northwestern frontier borders enemy states. For generations we have fought them and nursed grudges.

sentences.zh: 若男丁盡從軍，彼以兵來，則老弱必盡系累矣。

translations.literal: If all able-bodied men are taken into the army, when they come with troops the old and weak will surely all be captured and bound.
translations.idiomatic: If every fighting man is marched away and they attack, our elders, women, and children will all be taken captive.

sentences.zh: 幸使者入朝言之。

translations.literal: We hope the envoy will enter court and speak of this.
translations.idiomatic: We beg the envoy to go to court and report this for us.

sentences.zh: 」燥合畏罪不敢言，楊葛深念後西北有事得罪，遂以憂死。

translations.literal: " Zaohe feared punishment and dared not speak; Yang Ge Shen, brooding that later when trouble arose in the northwest he would be blamed, died of worry.
translations.idiomatic: " Zaohe feared punishment and kept silent. Yang Ge Shen, dreading that he would be held accountable when trouble broke out in the northwest, died of anxiety.

sentences.zh: 燥合複與牌印耶律娜、尚書省令史沒答涅合督起西北路兵。

translations.literal: Zaohe again, together with Paoyin Yelü Na and Ministry of Works clerk Modaniehe, supervised the mobilization of Northwestern Route troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zaohe again joined Paoyin Yelü Na and Ministry of Works clerk Modaniehe in mustering Northwestern Route forces.

sentences.zh: 契丹聞男丁當盡起，於是撒八、孛特補與部眾殺招討使完顏沃側及燥合，而執耶律娜、沒答涅合，取招討司貯甲三千，遂反。

translations.literal: When the Khitan heard that all able-bodied men were to be fully mobilized, Saba and Letebu with their tribal followers killed Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Woce and Zaohe, seized Yelü Na and Modaniehe, took three thousand suits of armor stored by the Pacification Commission, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that every fighting man was to be drafted, Saba and Letebu led their tribesmen in killing Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Woce and Zaohe, seizing Yelü Na and Modaniehe, stripping three thousand suits of armor from the Pacification Commission stores, and rising in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 議立豫王延禧子孫，眾推都監老和尚為招討使，山后四群牧、山前諸群牧皆應之。

translations.literal: They deliberated on enthroning a descendant of Prince Yu and Emperor Yanshi; the multitude pushed forward Supervisor Old Monk as pacification commissioner, and the four pasture offices beyond the mountains and the various pasture offices before the mountains all responded.
translations.idiomatic: They debated placing a descendant of Prince Yu and Emperor Yanshi on the throne. The rebels acclaimed Supervisor Old Monk as pacification commissioner, and the four pasture offices south of the mountains and all the pasture offices to the north joined them.

sentences.zh: 迪斡群牧使徒單賽裏、耶魯瓦群牧使鶴壽等皆遇害，語在《鶴壽傳》中。

translations.literal: Diwo Pasture Commissioner Tushan Saili, Yeluwa Pasture Commissioner He Shou, and others all met with violence; the account is in the "Biography of He Shou."
translations.idiomatic: Diwo Pasture Commissioner Tushan Saili, Yeluwa Pasture Commissioner He Shou, and others were killed; their story is told in the "Biography of He Shou."

sentences.zh: 五院司部人老和尚那也亦殺節度使術甲兀者以應撒八。

translations.literal: Old Monk Naye of the Wuyuan Office tribes also killed Military Commissioner Shujia Wuzhe to respond to Saba.
translations.idiomatic: Old Monk Naye of the Wuyuan Office tribes likewise killed Military Commissioner Shujia Wuzhe to join Saba's cause.

sentences.zh: 會甯八猛安牧馬於山后，至迪謀魯，賊盡奪其馬。

translations.literal: It happened that Ningba Meng'an was pasturing horses beyond the mountains; when he reached Dimolu, the rebels seized all his horses.
translations.idiomatic: Ningba Meng'an happened to be grazing horses in the southern hills. At Dimolu the rebels stripped him of every mount.

sentences.zh: 辟沙河千戶十哥等與前招討使完顏麻潑殺烏古迪列招討使烏林答蒲盧虎，以所部趨西北路。

translations.literal: Bisha River chiliarch Shige and others, together with former Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Mapo, killed Ughudilie Pacification Commissioner Ulin Da Puluhu and led their units toward the Northwestern Route.
translations.idiomatic: Bisha River chiliarch Shige and others joined former Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Mapo in killing Ughudilie Pacification Commissioner Ulin Da Puluhu, then marched their bands toward the Northwestern Route.

sentences.zh: 室魯部節度使阿廝列追擊敗之，十哥與數騎遁去，合於撒八。

translations.literal: Shilu Tribal Military Commissioner Asilie pursued, defeated them, and Shige fled with a few horsemen and joined Saba.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu Tribal Military Commissioner Asilie pursued and routed them. Shige escaped with a handful of riders and rejoined Saba.

sentences.zh: 咸平府謀克括裏，與所部自山后逃歸，咸平少尹完顏餘裏野欲收捕括裏家屬，括裏與其党招誘富家奴隸，數日得眾二千，遂攻陷韓州及柳河縣，遂趨咸平。

translations.literal: Xianping Prefecture company commander Kuoli, with his unit, fled back from beyond the mountains; Xianping Vice Prefect Wanyan Yuliye wished to seize Kuoli's family members. Kuoli with his faction recruited and enticed slaves of wealthy households; within days he gathered two thousand followers, then captured Han Prefecture and Liuhe County and pressed toward Xianping.
translations.idiomatic: Xianping Prefecture company commander Kuoli fled back from the southern hills with his band. When Xianping Vice Prefect Wanyan Yuliye moved to arrest Kuoli's kin, Kuoli and his confederates enticed slaves from wealthy households. Within days they mustered two thousand men, seized Han Prefecture and Liuhe County, and marched on Xianping.

sentences.zh: 餘裏野發兵迎擊之，兵敗，賊遂據咸平，於是繕完器甲，出府庫財物以募兵，賊勢益張。

translations.literal: Yuliye dispatched troops to meet and strike them; his army was defeated, and the rebels then occupied Xianping. Thereupon they repaired armor and weapons, spent the prefectural treasury to recruit troops, and the rebel power grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Yuliye marched out to intercept them but was defeated. The rebels took Xianping, repaired arms and armor, emptied the treasury to enlist men, and their strength swelled.

sentences.zh: 權曹家山猛安綽質，集兵千餘，扼幹夜河，賊不得東。

translations.literal: Acting Caojiashan Meng'an Chuo Zhi gathered more than a thousand troops, blocked Ganye River, and the rebels could not advance east.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Caojiashan Meng'an Chuo Zhi mustered more than a thousand men and held the Ganye River, blocking the rebels' eastward advance.

sentences.zh: 綽質兵敗，括裏遂犯濟州。

translations.literal: Chuo Zhi's army was defeated, and Kuoli then invaded Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo Zhi was defeated, and Kuoli turned to attack Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會宿直將軍孛術魯吳括剌徵兵于速頻路，遇括裏於信州，與猛安烏延查剌兵二千，擊敗括裏。

translations.literal: It happened that Palace Duty General Beshilu Wuguala was levying troops on the Supin Route; he encountered Kuoli at Xin Prefecture and, together with Meng'an Wuyan Zhala and two thousand troops, defeated Kuoli.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Duty General Beshilu Wuguala was raising troops on the Supin Route when he met Kuoli at Xin Prefecture. With Meng'an Wuyan Zhala and two thousand soldiers he routed Kuoli.

sentences.zh: 括裏收余眾趨東京，是時世宗為東京留守，以兵四百人拒之。

translations.literal: Kuoli gathered his remaining followers and hastened toward the Eastern Capital; at that time Shizong was military governor of the Eastern Capital and resisted with four hundred troops.
translations.idiomatic: Kuoli regrouped his survivors and struck for the Eastern Capital. Shizong, then military governor of the Eastern Capital, opposed him with four hundred men.

sentences.zh: 賊至常安縣，聞空中擊鼓聲如數千鼓者，候見旌旗蔽野，傳言留守以十萬兵至矣，即引還，亦以其眾合於撒八。

translations.literal: When the rebels reached Chang'an County, they heard in the air the sound of drums striking as though thousands of drums were beating; when scouts looked they saw banners covering the wilds, and rumor spread that the military governor had arrived with a hundred thousand troops. They at once withdrew and likewise joined their followers to Saba.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an County the rebels heard drumbeats in the air as if thousands were sounding together. Scouts reported banners blotting out the plain and rumor that the military governor had come with a hundred thousand men. They immediately retreated and merged their forces with Saba's.

sentences.zh: 海陵使樞密使僕散忽土、西京留守蕭懷忠將兵一萬，與右衛將軍蕭禿剌討平之。

translations.literal: The Hailing Emperor sent Privy Councilor Pusan Hutu and Western Capital Military Governor Xiao Huaizhong to lead ten thousand troops, together with Right Guard General Xiao Tula, to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The Hailing Emperor dispatched Privy Councilor Pusan Hutu and Western Capital Military Governor Xiao Huaizhong with ten thousand troops, along with Right Guard General Xiao Tula, to crush the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 禿剌與之相持數日，連與戰皆無功，而糧餉不繼，禿剌退歸臨潢。

translations.literal: Tula faced them for several days; repeated battles all achieved nothing, and supplies ran out, so Tula withdrew to Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Tula skirmished with them for days without success. When provisions failed he fell back to Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 禿剌雖不能克敵，而撒八自度大軍必相繼而至，勢不可支，謀歸於大石，乃率眾沿龍駒河西出。

translations.literal: Although Tula could not overcome the enemy, Saba reckoned that great armies would surely follow in succession and that the situation could not be sustained; he planned to submit to Dashi and therefore led his multitude westward along the Longju River.
translations.idiomatic: Though Tula could not break the rebels, Saba judged that imperial armies would keep coming and that he could not hold out. He resolved to join Dashi and led his followers west along the Longju River.

sentences.zh: 及僕散忽土、蕭懷忠等兵至，與禿剌合兵追至河上，不及而還。

translations.literal: When the troops of Pusan Hutu, Xiao Huaizhong, and others arrived and joined Tula in pursuit to the riverbank, they could not overtake them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Hutu and Xiao Huaizhong arrived and united with Tula to pursue the rebels to the river, but failed to catch them and turned back.

sentences.zh: 忽土、懷忠、禿剌坐逗遛不即追賊，皆誅死。

translations.literal: Hutu, Huaizhong, and Tula were punished for delay and for not pursuing the rebels at once; all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Hutu, Huaizhong, and Tula were condemned for dallying instead of pressing the pursuit and were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 北京留守蕭賾不能制其下，殺降人而取其婦女，亦坐誅。

translations.literal: Northern Capital Military Governor Xiao Ze could not control his subordinates; they killed surrendered men and took their women, and he too was punished with execution.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Capital Military Governor Xiao Ze failed to restrain his men, who murdered surrendered rebels and seized their women. He too was executed.

sentences.zh: 於是，白彥恭為北面兵馬都統，紇石烈志寧副之，守顏彀英為西北面兵馬都統，西北路招討使唐括孛姑的副之，以討撒八等。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bai Yangong was made northern frontier army commander-in-chief, with Heishilie Zhining as his deputy; Shouyan Gouying was made northwestern frontier army commander-in-chief, with Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Tanggu Bogede as his deputy, to campaign against Saba and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yangong was appointed northern frontier commander-in-chief with Heishilie Zhining as deputy. Shouyan Gouying became northwestern frontier commander-in-chief with Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Tanggu Bogede as deputy. They were sent to suppress Saba and his allies.

sentences.zh: 撒八既西行，而舊居山前者皆不欲往，偽署六院節度使移刺窩斡、兵官陳家殺撒八，執老和尚、孛特補等。

translations.literal: After Saba had marched west, those who had formerly lived before the mountains all did not wish to go; the falsely appointed Six-District Military Commissioner Yila Wo Wo and military officer Chen Jia killed Saba and seized Old Monk, Letebu, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Once Saba marched west, his followers from the northern country refused to follow. The rebels' Six-District Military Commissioner Yila Wo Wo and military officer Chen Jia killed Saba and seized Old Monk, Letebu, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 至是，窩斡始自為都元帥，陳家為都監，擁眾東還，至臨潢府東南新羅寨。

translations.literal: At this point Wo Wo for the first time made himself grand marshal, with Chen Jia as chief supervisor; he led his multitude back east to Xinluo Stockade southeast of Linhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo then declared himself grand marshal and made Chen Jia chief supervisor. He led his followers back east as far as Xinluo Stockade southeast of Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 世宗使移剌紮八、前押軍謀克播斡、前牌印麻駭、利涉軍節度判官馬腦等招之。

translations.literal: Shizong sent Yila Zhahe, former Escort Army company commander Bowo, former Paoyin Mahai, and Lishe Army military commissioner judge Ma Nao and others to summon them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong dispatched Yila Zhahe, former Escort Army company commander Bowo, former Paoyin Mahai, and Lishe Army commissioner judge Ma Nao to offer terms of surrender.

sentences.zh: 紮八等見窩斡，以上意諭之。

translations.literal: Zhahe and the others saw Wo Wo and explained the emperor's intent to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhahe and his party met Wo Wo and conveyed the emperor's message.

sentences.zh: 窩斡已約降，已而複謂紮八曰：「若降，爾能保我輩無事乎？

translations.literal: Wo Wo had already agreed to surrender, but then again said to Zhahe: "If we surrender, can you guarantee that we will come to no harm?
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo had already agreed to submit, but then asked Zhahe, "If we surrender, can you guarantee our safety?

sentences.zh: 」紮八曰：「我知招降耳，其他豈能必哉。」

translations.literal: " Zhahe said: "I know only how to summon men to surrender; as for the rest, how can I be certain?"
translations.idiomatic: " Zhahe replied, "My charge is to offer surrender. Beyond that I can promise nothing."

sentences.zh: 紮八見窩斡兵眾強，車帳滿野，意其可以有成，因說之曰：「我之始來，以汝輩不能有為，今觀兵勢強盛如此，汝等欲如群羊為人所驅去乎，將欲待天時乎？

translations.literal: Zhahe saw that Wo Wo's troops were strong and carts and tents filled the wilds; he thought they might succeed and therefore urged him, saying: "When I first came I thought you could accomplish nothing; now seeing your military strength so great, do you wish to be like a flock of sheep driven away by others, or do you intend to await Heaven's season?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Wo Wo's strength — carts and tents covering the plain — Zhahe decided the rebels might yet prevail and urged him: "When I arrived I thought you could achieve nothing. Yet your host is this powerful. Will you go like sheep driven by others, or wait upon Heaven's moment?

sentences.zh: 若果有大志，吾亦不復還矣。

translations.literal: If you truly have great ambition, I too will not return.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly mean to fight on, I will not return either.

sentences.zh: 」賊將有前孛特本部族節度使逐斡者，言：「昔谷神丞相，賢能人也，嘗說他日西北部族當有事。

translations.literal: " Among the rebel generals was the former Letebu Tribal Military Commissioner Zhuwozhe, who said: "In former times Chancellor Gushen, a man of talent and ability, once said that someday the northwestern tribes would have trouble.
translations.idiomatic: " Rebel general Zhuwozhe, formerly Letebu's tribal military commissioner, spoke up: "Chancellor Gushen was a wise man. He once said the northwestern tribes would one day rise.

sentences.zh: 今日正合此語，恐不可降也。

translations.literal: Today this saying fits exactly; I fear we cannot surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Today his words have come true. I fear we must not surrender.

sentences.zh: 」於是，窩斡遂決意不復肯降矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Wo Wo resolved at last that he would no longer consent to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " Wo Wo then made up his mind never to submit.

sentences.zh: 紮八亦留賊中，惟麻駭、播斡還歸。

translations.literal: Zhahe also remained among the rebels; only Mahai and Bowo returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhahe stayed with the rebels. Only Mahai and Bowo came back.

sentences.zh: 窩斡乃引兵攻臨潢府，總管移室懣出城戰，兵少被執，賊遂圍臨潢，眾至五萬。

translations.literal: Wo Wo then led troops to attack Linhuang Prefecture; Commander Yishi Men went out to fight, but with too few troops was captured. The rebels then besieged Linhuang, and their numbers reached fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo marched on Linhuang. Commander Yishi Men sallied out to fight but was captured when his force proved too small. The rebels besieged the city until their numbers swelled to fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 正隆六年十二月己亥，窩斡遂稱帝，改元天正。

translations.literal: On the jihai day of the twelfth month of the sixth year of Zhenglong, Wo Wo then declared himself emperor and changed the era name to Tianzheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day of the twelfth month of Zhenglong 6, Wo Wo proclaimed himself emperor and adopted the era name Tianzheng.

sentences.zh: 是時，北面都統白彥敬、副統紇石烈志寧在北京，聞世宗即位，以兵來歸。

translations.literal: At that time Northern Frontier Commander-in-Chief Bai Yanjing and Deputy Commander Heishilie Zhining were at the Northern Capital; hearing that Shizong had ascended the throne, they came with their troops to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Frontier Commander-in-Chief Bai Yanjing and Deputy Commander Heishilie Zhining were then at the Northern Capital. Learning of Shizong's accession, they marched south to join him.

sentences.zh: 世宗使元帥左都監吾紮忽、同知北京留守事完顏骨只救臨潢，晝夜兼行，比至臨潢，賊已解圍去攻泰州。

translations.literal: Shizong sent Grand Marshal Left Overseer Wuzhahu and Northern Capital Military Governor Vice Commissioner Wanyan Guzhi to relieve Linhuang; they marched day and night without rest, but by the time they reached Linhuang the rebels had already lifted the siege and gone to attack Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent Grand Marshal Left Overseer Wuzhahu and Northern Capital co-governor Wanyan Guzhi to relieve Linhuang. They forced the march day and night, but when they arrived the rebels had already abandoned the siege and moved against Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 吾紮忽追及於窊曆，兩軍已陣將戰，押軍猛安契丹忽剌叔以所部兵應賊，吾紮忽軍遂敗。

translations.literal: Wuzhahu overtook them at Walie; the two armies had already formed ranks and were about to fight when Escort Army Meng'an Khitan Hulashu with his unit responded to the rebels, and Wuzhahu's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhahu caught up with them at Walie. The two armies were forming for battle when Escort Army Meng'an Khitan Hulashu went over to the rebels with his command, and Wuzhahu's force was routed.

sentences.zh: 泰州節度使烏裏雅率千餘騎與窩斡遇，烏裏雅兵複敗，僅以數騎脫歸。

translations.literal: Taizhou Military Commissioner Wuliya led more than a thousand horsemen and encountered Wo Wo; Wuliya's army was again defeated, and he escaped back with only a few riders.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou Military Commissioner Wuliya met Wo Wo with more than a thousand cavalry but was beaten again and fled home with only a few companions.

sentences.zh: 賊勢愈振，城中震駭，莫敢出戰。

translations.literal: The rebel power grew ever stronger; the city was shaken with terror and none dared go out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' momentum swelled. Terror gripped the city and no one dared sally forth.

sentences.zh: 賊四面登城，押軍猛安烏古孫阿裏補率軍士數人，各持刀以身率先循城擊賊力戰，斫刈甚眾，賊乃退走，城賴以完。

translations.literal: The rebels climbed the walls on all four sides. Escort Army Meng'an Wugusun Alibu led several soldiers, each holding a blade and taking the lead in person along the wall to strike the rebels and fight fiercely; they cut down many, and the rebels then retreated. The city was preserved thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels scaled the walls on every side. Escort Army Meng'an Wugusun Alibu led a handful of soldiers along the ramparts, blades in hand, cutting down many rebels until they withdrew. The city was saved.

sentences.zh: 泰州司吏顏盞蒲查奏捷，除忠翊校尉，賜銀五十兩、重彩十端。

translations.literal: Taizhou clerk Yanshan Pucha reported the victory; he was appointed Loyal Assistant Commandant and granted fifty taels of silver and ten bolts of heavy silk.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou clerk Yanshan Pucha reported the victory. He was made Loyal Assistant Commandant and rewarded with fifty taels of silver and ten bolts of fine silk.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，右副元帥完顏謀衍率諸軍北征窩斡。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Right Deputy Grand Marshal Wanyan Moyan Yan led the various armies on a northern expedition against Wo Wo.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 2, Right Deputy Grand Marshal Wanyan Moyan Yan led the combined armies north against Wo Wo.

sentences.zh: 二月壬戌詔曰：「應諸人若能於契丹賊中自拔歸者，更不問元初首從及被威脅之由，奴婢、良人罪無輕重並行免放。

translations.literal: On the renxu day of the second month an edict said: "All persons who can extricate themselves from among the Khitan rebels and return shall no longer be questioned about whether they were original ringleaders or followers, nor about having been coerced; slaves and commoners, whatever the weight of their offenses, shall all alike be pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day of the second month an edict declared: "Anyone who breaks away from the Khitan rebels and returns shall not be questioned about original guilt, leadership, or coercion. Slaves and commoners alike, whatever their offense, shall be pardoned and freed.

sentences.zh: 曾有官職及糾率人眾來歸者，仍與官賞，依本品量材敘使。

translations.literal: Those who formerly held office and those who gathered and led people to return shall still receive official rewards and be assigned posts according to their former rank and measured by their talent.
translations.idiomatic: Former officials and those who bring followers back shall receive offices and rewards commensurate with their former rank and ability.

sentences.zh: 其同來人各從所願處收系，有才能者亦與錄用。

translations.literal: Those who come together with them shall each be registered wherever they wish, and those with ability shall also be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Their companions may settle wherever they choose, and capable men among them shall be given posts.

sentences.zh: 內外官員郎君群牧直撒百姓人家驅奴、宮籍監人等，並放為良，亦從所願處收系，與免三年差役。

translations.literal: Inner and outer officials, langjun, pasture-household commoners, household slaves, palace-registry overseers, and the like shall all be released as commoners, likewise registered wherever they wish, and granted exemption from corvée for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Inner and outer officials, langjun, pasture-household commoners, household slaves, palace-registry overseers, and the like shall all be freed to commoner status, registered where they choose, and exempted from corvée for three years.

sentences.zh: 或能捕殺首領而歸者，准上施行，仍驗勞績約量遷賞。

translations.literal: If any can capture or kill rebel leaders and return, the above provisions shall apply, and rewards and promotions shall be measured according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Those who capture or kill rebel leaders shall receive the rewards above, with promotion scaled to their deeds.

sentences.zh: 如捕獲窩斡者，猛安加三品官授節度使，謀克加四品官授防禦使，庶人加五品官授刺史。

translations.literal: If Wo Wo is captured, a meng'an shall be raised three ranks and appointed military commissioner, a company commander raised four ranks and appointed defense commissioner, and a commoner raised five ranks and appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever captures Wo Wo shall receive a meng'an promotion of three ranks to military commissioner, a company commander promotion of four ranks to defense commissioner, or a commoner promotion of five ranks to prefect.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「尚書省，如節度防禦使捉獲窩斡者與世襲猛安，刺史捉獲者與世襲謀克，驅奴、宮籍監人亦與庶人同。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Ministry of Works: if a military or defense commissioner captures Wo Wo, grant an hereditary meng'an; if a prefect captures him, grant an hereditary company command; household slaves and palace-registry overseers shall receive the same as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: " Another edict instructed the Ministry of Works: "A military or defense commissioner who captures Wo Wo shall receive an hereditary meng'an; a prefect who captures him shall receive an hereditary company command. Household slaves and palace-registry overseers shall be rewarded like commoners.

sentences.zh: 」複詔宰臣，遍諭將士，能捕殺窩斡者加特進、授真總管。

translations.literal: " Again the chief ministers were edicted to proclaim throughout to officers and soldiers that whoever could capture or kill Wo Wo would receive the extraordinary promotion and be appointed true commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief ministers were further ordered to announce to every officer and soldier that whoever captured or killed Wo Wo would receive extraordinary promotion and appointment as commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 於是，括裏將犯韓州，聞元帥兵至，不戰遁去，將轉趨懿、宜州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kuoli was about to invade Han Prefecture; hearing that the grand marshal's troops had arrived, he fled without fighting and was about to turn toward Yi and Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kuoli was marching on Han Prefecture when news of the grand marshal's approach sent him fleeing without a fight. He turned toward Yi and Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 謀衍屯懿州慶雲縣，及屯川州武平縣，奏請糧運當遣人護送，兵仗乞選精良者付之。

translations.literal: Moyan Yan encamped at Qingyun County in Yi Prefecture and at Wuping County in Chuan Prefecture, memorializing that grain transport should be sent with escorts and requesting that choice weapons be issued to them.
translations.idiomatic: Moyan Yan encamped at Qingyun County in Yi Prefecture and Wuping County in Chuan Prefecture. He memorialized that grain convoys required escorts and asked that the best arms be issued to them.

sentences.zh: 詔以南征逃還軍士就往屯戍，如不足，量于富家簽調，就近地簽步軍，給仗護送糧運。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that soldiers who had fled back from the southern campaign be sent directly to garrison duty; if insufficient, wealthy households were to be levied proportionately, and infantry conscripted locally, with arms issued to escort grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered soldiers who had deserted the southern campaign assigned to garrison duty. If their numbers fell short, levies would be drawn from wealthy households and local infantry conscripted nearby, armed and sent to guard the grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 詔平章政事移剌元宜往泰州規措邊事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Grand Councilor Yila Yuanyi to go to Taizhou to arrange frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Yila Yuanyi was ordered to Taizhou to manage frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 前安遠大將軍斡裏嫋、猛安七斤、庶人阿裏葛、磨哥等自窩斡中來降，斡裏嫋、七斤加昭武大將軍，阿裏葛武義將軍，磨哥忠勇校尉。

translations.literal: Former Anyuan General Woli Niao, Meng'an Qijin, commoner Alige, Moge, and others came to surrender from Wo Wo's camp; Woli Niao and Qijin were promoted to Illustrious Martial General, Alige to Martial Righteousness General, and Moge to Loyal Valor Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Former Anyuan General Woli Niao, Meng'an Qijin, commoners Alige and Moge, and others defected from Wo Wo's camp. Woli Niao and Qijin were made Illustrious Martial Generals, Alige Martial Righteousness General, and Moge Loyal Valor Commandant.

sentences.zh: 窩斡遂自泰州往攻濟州，欲邀糧運。

translations.literal: Wo Wo then marched from Taizhou to attack Ji Prefecture, intending to intercept grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo left Taizhou to strike Ji Prefecture, aiming to cut the grain route.

sentences.zh: 元帥完顏謀衍與右監軍完顏福壽、左都監吾紮忽合兵，甲士萬三千人，曷懶路總管徒單克甯、廣甯尹僕散渾坦、同知廣甯尹完顏岩雅、肇州防禦使唐括烏也為左翼，臨海節度使紇石烈志寧、曷速館節度使神土懣、同知北京留守完顏骨只、淄州刺史尼龐古鈔兀為右翼，至術虎崖，盡委輜重，士卒齎數日糧，輕騎襲之。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Wanyan Moyan Yan joined forces with Right Overseer Wanyan Fushou and Left Overseer Wuzhahu, ten thousand three hundred armored soldiers in all. Supin Route Commander Tushan Kening, Guangning Prefect Pusan Huntan, Guangning Vice Prefect Wanyan Yanya, and Zhao Prefecture Defense Commissioner Tanggu Wuye formed the left wing; Linhai Military Commissioner Heishilie Zhining, Yisuguan Military Commissioner Shen Tu Men, Northern Capital co-governor Wanyan Guzhi, and Zibo Prefect Nipanggu Chaowu formed the right wing. Reaching Shuhu Cliff, they left all baggage behind; soldiers carried several days' rations and light cavalry struck in a raid.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Wanyan Moyan Yan united with Right Overseer Wanyan Fushou and Left Overseer Wuzhahu — thirteen thousand armored men in all. Supin Route Commander Tushan Kening, Guangning Prefect Pusan Huntan, Guangning Vice Prefect Wanyan Yanya, and Zhao Defense Commissioner Tanggu Wuye led the left wing. Linhai Military Commissioner Heishilie Zhining, Yisuguan Military Commissioner Shen Tu Men, Northern Capital co-governor Wanyan Guzhi, and Zibo Prefect Nipanggu Chaowu led the right. At Shuhu Cliff they abandoned their baggage train, each man carrying several days' grain, and swept down in a light-cavalry raid.

sentences.zh: 糺椀群牧人契丹颭者，與其弟孛迭、挼剌，皆棄家自賊中來降。

translations.literal: Jiuwan Pasture Khitan Zhanzhe, together with his younger brothers Bedie and Ruola, all abandoned their families and came to surrender from the rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuwan Pasture Khitan Zhanzhe and his brothers Bedie and Ruola abandoned their families and defected from the rebels.

sentences.zh: 糺者謂謀衍曰：「賊中馬肥健，官軍馬疲弱，此去賊八十里，比遇賊馬已憊。

translations.literal: Zhanzhe said to Moyan Yan: "The rebels' horses are fat and strong; the government army's horses are weak and exhausted. The rebels are eighty li from here; by the time we meet them their horses will already be weary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhe told Moyan Yan, "The rebels' horses are strong and ours are spent. They are eighty li away — by the time we reach them their mounts will be exhausted.

sentences.zh: 賊輜重去此不遠，我攻之，賊必救其巢穴，賊至馬必疲，我馬少得息，所謂攻其所必救，以逸待勞者也。

translations.literal: The rebels' baggage is not far from here; if we attack it they will surely rescue their nest. When the rebels arrive their horses will be weary while ours will have had a little rest — this is what is called attacking where they must rescue and awaiting the weary with the rested.
translations.idiomatic: Their baggage train is close by. Strike it and they must turn back to save their camp. When they arrive their horses will be blown and ours will have rested — attack where they must respond and meet fatigue with fresh strength.

sentences.zh: 」謀衍從之，乘夜亟發，會大風路暗不能辨，遲明行三十里許，與賊輜重相近，整兵少憩。

translations.literal: " Moyan Yan followed this advice and set out urgently by night; they encountered great wind and dark roads and could not distinguish the way. At dawn they had marched about thirty li and were near the rebels' baggage; they ordered the troops and rested briefly.
translations.idiomatic: " Moyan Yan agreed and marched through the night. A gale and darkness made the road impossible to follow. At dawn, after some thirty li, they drew near the rebel baggage train, reformed ranks, and rested briefly.

sentences.zh: 窩斡趨濟州，知大軍取其輜重，乃還救，遇於長濼。

translations.literal: Wo Wo was pressing toward Ji Prefecture; learning that the great army was taking his baggage, he turned back to rescue it and met them at Chang Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo was hurrying toward Ji Prefecture when he learned the imperial army had seized his baggage. He wheeled about to save it and met them at Chang Marsh.

sentences.zh: 既陣，謀衍別設伏於左翼之側，賊四百餘騎突出左翼伏兵之間，徒單克寧射卻之。

translations.literal: Once ranks were formed, Moyan Yan separately set an ambush on the flank of the left wing; more than four hundred rebel horsemen burst out between the left-wing ambush, and Tushan Kening shot them back.
translations.idiomatic: As the armies formed, Moyan Yan hid troops beside the left wing. More than four hundred rebel horsemen burst through the gap, but Tushan Kening drove them back with arrows.

sentences.zh: 是日，別部諸將與賊對者，勝負未分，相去五里許而立。

translations.literal: That day the various generals of the separate divisions facing the rebels had not yet decided victory or defeat and stood about five li apart.
translations.idiomatic: That day the detached commanders facing the rebels were still locked in stalemate, their lines some five li apart.

sentences.zh: 左翼萬戶襄別與賊戰，賊陣動，襄麾軍乘之，突出其後，俱與大軍不相及。

translations.literal: Left-wing chiliarch Xiang Bie fought the rebels; the rebel formation shifted, and Xiang waved his army to press the advantage, bursting out behind them, and both sides lost contact with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Left-wing chiliarch Xiang Bie engaged the rebels. When their line wavered he signaled the charge and broke through behind them, leaving both his command and the main army out of contact.

sentences.zh: 襄以善射者二十騎，率眾自賊後擊之，賊不能支，乘勢麾軍擊其一偏，賊遂卻。

translations.literal: Xiang with twenty skilled archers on horseback led the multitude to strike them from the rear; the rebels could not hold, and seizing the momentum he waved his army to attack one flank, and the rebels then retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang took twenty expert archers and struck from the rear. The rebels buckled. He pressed the advantage, smashed one flank, and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 襄遂與大軍合，而別部諸將皆至，整陣力戰，忽反風揚砂石，賊陣亂，官軍馳擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Xiang then rejoined the main army, and the generals of the separate divisions all arrived; they ordered ranks and fought fiercely. Suddenly a reverse wind raised sand and stones, the rebel formation fell into disorder, and the government army charged and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang rejoined the main force as the detached commanders closed in. They reformed and fought hard until a sudden reverse wind whipped sand and gravel into the rebel ranks. The imperial cavalry charged and broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 追北十餘裏，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: They pursued the fleeing enemy more than ten li and killed and captured a great multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran more than ten li, with heavy slaughter and many captives.

sentences.zh: 詔以糺者為武義將軍，孛迭昭信校尉，挼剌忠翊校尉。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhanzhe Martial Righteousness General, Bedie Trusted Faith Commandant, and Ruola Loyal Assistant Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhe was made Martial Righteousness General, Bedie Trusted Faith Commandant, and Ruola Loyal Assistant Commandant.

sentences.zh: 糺除同知建州事，未之官，卒。

translations.literal: Zhanzhe was appointed Vice Commissioner of Jian Prefecture affairs but died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanzhe was appointed vice commissioner of Jian Prefecture but died before assuming the post.

sentences.zh: 孛迭取家賊中，遂被害，上憫之，後以挼剌為汝州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Bedie went to fetch his family from the rebel camp and was thereupon killed; the emperor pitied him, and later appointed Ruola Chief Inspector of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bedie returned to the rebel camp to fetch his family and was killed. The emperor mourned him and later made Ruola Chief Inspector of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 窩斡率其眾西走，謀衍追及之於霿𩃭河。

translations.literal: Wo Wo led his multitude fleeing west; Moyan Yan overtook him at the Menglong River.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo fled west with his followers. Moyan Yan caught up with him at the Menglong River.

sentences.zh: 賊已濟，毀其津口，紇石烈志寧軍先至，不克渡，乃對岸為疑兵，以夾穀清臣、徒單海羅兩萬戶於下流渡河，值支港兩岸鬥絕且濘淖，命軍士束柳填港而過。

translations.literal: The rebels had already crossed and destroyed the ford. Heishilie Zhining's army arrived first but could not cross; he therefore made a feint on the opposite bank and sent chiliarchs Jiagu Qingchen and Tushan Hailuo to cross downstream. They encountered branch channels whose banks were steep and miry, and he ordered soldiers to bundle willows and fill the channels to pass.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had crossed and wrecked the ford. Zhining's vanguard arrived first but could not follow. He feinted from the far bank while chiliarchs Jiagu Qingchen and Tushan Hailuo forded downstream. Where side channels ran deep and miry between steep banks, he had his men bundle willows and fill the channels to cross.

sentences.zh: 追之數裏，得平地，方食，賊眾奄至。

translations.literal: After pursuing several li they reached level ground and were just eating when the rebel multitude suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued several li to open ground and had just begun to eat when the rebels fell upon them.

sentences.zh: 志寧軍急整陣，賊自南岡馳下，沖陣者三，志寧力戰，流矢中左臂，戰自若。

translations.literal: Zhining's army hurriedly ordered ranks; the rebels galloped down from the southern ridge and charged the formation three times. Zhining fought fiercely; a stray arrow struck his left arm, yet he fought as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining's men scrambled into formation as rebels charged down the southern ridge three times. An arrow struck Zhining's left arm, but he fought on as if untouched.

sentences.zh: 大軍畢至，左翼騎兵先與賊接，賊據上風縱火，乘煙擊官軍，官軍步兵亦至，並力合戰，凡十余合，軍士苦風煙皆植立如癡。

translations.literal: When the main army had all arrived, the left-wing cavalry first engaged the rebels. The rebels held the upwind position and set fires, striking the government army through the smoke. The government infantry also arrived, and all joined in battle for more than ten rounds; the soldiers suffered from wind and smoke and stood rooted like men in a daze.
translations.idiomatic: The main force arrived and the left-wing cavalry engaged first. The rebels held the windward ground, set fires, and struck through the smoke. Imperial infantry joined the fight. For more than ten clashes the soldiers choked on wind and smoke and stood dazed as if stunned.

sentences.zh: 會天降雨，風止，官軍奮擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Heaven sent rain; the wind stopped, and the government army struck with vigor and routed them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell, the wind died, and the imperial army surged forward to crush them.

sentences.zh: 徒單克寧追奔十五里，賊前厄溪澗不得亟渡，多殺傷。

translations.literal: Tushan Kening pursued the fleeing enemy fifteen li; the rebels were blocked ahead by streams and ravines and could not cross quickly, and many were killed and wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Tushan Kening pursued fifteen li. Streams and gullies blocked the rebels' path and many were cut down before they could cross.

sentences.zh: 賊既渡，官軍亦渡，少憩，賊反旆來攻，克甯以大軍不繼，令軍士皆下馬射賊。

translations.literal: After the rebels had crossed, the government army also crossed and rested briefly. The rebels turned their banners and came to attack; Kening, because the main army had not followed, ordered the soldiers all to dismount and shoot the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels had crossed, the imperial troops followed and paused briefly. The rebels wheeled about and attacked. With the main army not yet up, Kening ordered his men to dismount and shoot.

sentences.zh: 賊引卻而南，克寧亦將引而北，士未及騎馬，賊複來衝突，官軍少卻，回渡澗北。

translations.literal: The rebels withdrew southward, and Kening was also about to withdraw northward; the men had not yet remounted when the rebels again came charging. The government army fell back slightly and recrossed to the north of the stream.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pulled back south. Kening prepared to withdraw north, but before his men could remount the rebels charged again. The imperial line gave ground and fell back across the stream.

sentences.zh: 大軍至，賊遂引去。

translations.literal: When the main army arrived, the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army arrived the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 四月，詔元帥府曰；

translations.literal: In the fourth month an edict addressed the Grand Marshal's headquarters, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the court addressed the Grand Marshal's headquarters:

sentences.zh: 「應契丹賊人，與大兵未戰已前投降者，不得殺傷，仍加安撫。

translations.literal: "All Khitan rebels who surrender before engaging the great army in battle shall not be killed or harmed, and shall still receive reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: "Khitan rebels who surrender before battle with the main army must not be harmed and shall be treated with leniency.

sentences.zh: 敗走以後，招誘來降者，除奴婢准已虜為定外，親屬分付圓聚。

translations.literal: Those who after defeat and flight are summoned and enticed to surrender, except for slaves and maidservants who shall be fixed according to those already captured, shall have their kin assigned and gathered together.
translations.idiomatic: Those who surrender after defeat shall have their kin reunited, except for slaves and maidservants already taken captive.

sentences.zh: 仍官為換贖。」

translations.literal: The government shall still redeem them on their behalf."
translations.idiomatic: The state shall redeem them where ransom is required."

sentences.zh: 窩斡既敗，謀衍不復追討，駐軍白濼。

translations.literal: After Wo Wo was defeated, Moyan Yan no longer pursued and punished them, but encamped at Bai Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: After Wo Wo's defeat Moyan Yan ceased pursuit and encamped at Bai Marsh.

sentences.zh: 窩斡攻懿州不克，遂殘破川州，將遁於山西，而北京亦不邀擊之。

translations.literal: Wo Wo attacked Yi Prefecture without success, then ravaged Chuan Prefecture and was about to flee into the western mountains, yet the Northern Capital also did not intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo failed to take Yi Prefecture, ravaged Chuan Prefecture, and prepared to escape into the western hills. The Northern Capital force did not intercept him.

sentences.zh: 於是，發驍騎軍二千、曷懶路留屯京師軍三千，號稱二萬，會寧濟州軍六千亦號二萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon two thousand crack cavalry were dispatched, and three thousand troops of the Supin Route garrison left at the capital were called twenty thousand; together with six thousand troops of the Huining and Ji Prefecture armies, also called twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand crack cavalry were mobilized, and three thousand Supin Route troops left in the capital were reported as twenty thousand. Six thousand men from Huining and Ji Prefecture were likewise counted as twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 元帥左都監高忠建總兵，沃州刺史烏古論蒲查為曷懶路押軍萬戶，祁州刺史烏林答剌撒為濟州押軍萬戶，右驍騎副都指揮使烏延查剌為驍騎萬戶，祁州刺史宗甯為會甯路押軍萬戶，右宣徽使宗亨為北京路都統，吏部郎中完顏達吉為副統，會元帥府討擊之。
