translations.literal: Grand Marshal Left Overseer Gao Zhongjian commanded the troops overall; Wo Prefect Wugulun Pucha was Supin Route Escort Army chiliarch, Qi Prefect Ulin Da Lasa was Ji Prefecture Escort Army chiliarch, Right Crack-Cavalry Deputy Commander Wuyan Zhala was crack-cavalry chiliarch, Qi Prefect Zong Ning was Huining Route Escort Army chiliarch, Right Palace Commissioner Zong Heng was Northern Capital Route commander-in-chief, and Ministry of Personnel director Wanyan Daji was deputy commander. They joined the Grand Marshal's headquarters to pursue and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Left Overseer Gao Zhongjian took overall command. Wo Prefect Wugulun Pucha became Supin Route Escort Army chiliarch, Qi Prefect Ulin Da Lasa Ji Prefecture Escort Army chiliarch, Right Crack-Cavalry Deputy Commander Wuyan Zhala crack-cavalry chiliarch, and Qi Prefect Zong Ning Huining Route Escort Army chiliarch. Right Palace Commissioner Zong Heng became Northern Capital Route commander-in-chief with Ministry of Personnel director Wanyan Daji as deputy. They joined the Grand Marshal's headquarters to hunt the rebels.

sentences.zh: 詔使尚廄局副使蒲察蒲盧渾往懿州戒敕將帥，上曰：「朕委卿等討賊，乃聞不就賊趨戰，而駐兵閑緩，經涉累月，雖曾追襲，乃不由有水草之地，以致馬疲弱不能百里而還。

translations.literal: The edict envoy, Imperial Stud Deputy Commissioner Pucha Puluhun, was sent to Yi Prefecture to admonish the generals. The emperor said: "I entrusted you to suppress the rebels, yet I hear you do not press toward the enemy to fight, but encamp at leisure and delay, passing many months. Although you once pursued and raided, you did not go by lands with water and fodder, so that the horses grew weak and exhausted and could not return after a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Stud Deputy Commissioner Pucha Puluhun was sent to Yi Prefecture to rebuke the commanders. The emperor said, "I entrusted you with suppressing the rebels, yet you linger in camp instead of closing with the enemy. Months have passed. Though you pursued once, you avoided watered pasture and ruined your horses so they could not ride a hundred li and return.

sentences.zh: 後雖破賊，而縱諸軍劫掠，數日後方追北霿𩃭河，亦不乘勝，輒複引還。

translations.literal: Later, although you defeated the rebels, you allowed the various armies to plunder; only after several days did you pursue north to the Menglong River, and again you did not press the victory but promptly withdrew once more.
translations.idiomatic: Later, though you broke the rebels, you let your troops plunder. Only days afterward did you pursue to the Menglong River, and even then you failed to press the advantage and withdrew again.

sentences.zh: 賊遂入涉近地，北京、懿州由此受兵。

translations.literal: The rebels then entered and troubled nearby lands; the Northern Capital and Yi Prefecture thereby suffered attack.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then raided the nearby country, and the Northern Capital and Yi Prefecture bore the brunt.

sentences.zh: 朕欲重譴汝等，以方任兵事，且圖後功。

translations.literal: I wished to punish you severely, but since you are still entrusted with military affairs, I look instead to your later achievements.
translations.idiomatic: I would have punished you severely, but with war still in hand I withhold judgment and look to your future service.

sentences.zh: 當盡心一力，毋得似前怠弛。

translations.literal: You must devote your hearts and united strength and must not be slack as before.
translations.idiomatic: Devote yourselves wholly and do not repeat your former slackness.

sentences.zh: 」上謂蒲盧渾曰：「卿若聞賊在近，即當監督討伐。

translations.literal: " The emperor said to Puluhun: "If you hear the rebels are near, you must at once supervise their suppression.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor told Puluhun, "When you hear the rebels are near, you must oversee the campaign yourself.

sentences.zh: 用命力戰者疏記以聞，朕將約量遷賞。

translations.literal: Those who obey orders and fight fiercely — record them in memorial and report; I shall measure rewards and promotions accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Record those who obey orders and fight hard, report them to me, and I shall reward them according to their merit.

sentences.zh: 無或承徇上官，抑有功、濫署無功者。

translations.literal: There must be none who, currying favor with superiors, suppress the meritorious or indiscriminately assign honors to the undeserving.
translations.idiomatic: None of you must curry favor with your superiors by suppressing the meritorious or recklessly crediting the undeserving.

sentences.zh: 善戢士卒、勿縱虜掠。

translations.literal: Restrain the soldiers well and do not allow plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Keep your troops disciplined and do not permit looting.

sentences.zh: 」以紇石烈志甯為元帥右監軍，右副元帥完顏謀衍、元帥右監軍完顏福壽召還京師，咸平路總管完顏兀帶復舊職。

translations.literal: " Heishilie Zhining was made Grand Marshal Right Overseer; Right Deputy Grand Marshal Wanyan Moyan Yan and Grand Marshal Right Overseer Wanyan Fushou were recalled to the capital; Xianping Route commander Wanyan Wudai was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: " Heishilie Zhining was appointed Grand Marshal Right Overseer. Right Deputy Grand Marshal Wanyan Moyan Yan and Grand Marshal Right Overseer Wanyan Fushou were recalled to the capital, and Xianping Route commander Wanyan Wudai was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 謀衍男斜哥在軍中多暴橫，詔押歸本管。

translations.literal: Moyan Yan's son Xiege behaved with much violence and bullying in the army; an edict ordered him detained and sent back to his original jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Moyan Yan's son Xiege had been brutal and overbearing in the army. The court ordered him arrested and returned to his home command.

sentences.zh: 窩斡使所親招節度使移裏堇窟域，窟域執其使送官，與窩斡連戰有功，遷宣武將軍，賜銀五百兩、衣二襲。

translations.literal: Wo Wo sent an intimate to summon Military Commissioner Yiliqin Kuyu; Kuyu seized the envoy and sent him to the authorities. Because he had repeatedly fought Wo Wo with merit, he was promoted to Xuanwu General and granted five hundred taels of silver and two suits of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo sent a trusted agent to summon Military Commissioner Yiliqin Kuyu, but Kuyu seized the envoy and delivered him to the authorities. For repeated victories over Wo Wo he was promoted to Xuanwu General and rewarded with five hundred taels of silver and two suits of clothing.

sentences.zh: 起運在中都弓萬五千、箭一百五十萬赴懿州。

translations.literal: Bow transport was raised from the Central Capital — fifteen thousand bows and one million five hundred thousand arrows — to be sent to Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen thousand bows and a million and a half arrows were shipped from the Central Capital to Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 平章政事移剌元宜、甯昌軍節度使宗敘入見，詔使自中道卻還軍中，宣諭元宜、謀衍注意經略邊事。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Yila Yuanyi and Ningchang Army Military Commissioner Zong Xu were received in audience; the edict ordered them to return midway to the army and instructed Yuanyi and Moyan Yan to attend to frontier strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Yila Yuanyi and Ningchang Army Military Commissioner Zong Xu were summoned to court, then ordered to turn back and return to their commands. Yuanyi and Moyan Yan were instructed to devote themselves to frontier strategy.

sentences.zh: 師久無功，尚書右丞僕散忠義願效死力除邊患，世宗嘉歎。

translations.literal: The campaign had dragged on without success; Ministry of Works Right Vice Commissioner Pusan Zhongyi offered to devote his life to removing the frontier threat, and Shizong praised him with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign had dragged on without victory. Right Vice Commissioner of the Ministry of Works Pusan Zhongyi volunteered to stake his life on clearing the frontier threat. Shizong praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 六月，忠義拜平章政事兼右副元帥，宗敘為兵部尚書，各賜弓矢、具鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Zhongyi was appointed Grand Councilor concurrently Right Deputy Grand Marshal; Zong Xu was made Minister of War; each was granted bow and arrows and a fully saddled and bridled horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zhongyi became Grand Councilor and Right Deputy Grand Marshal. Zong Xu was made Minister of War. Both received bows, arrows, and fully equipped horses.

sentences.zh: 出內府金銀十萬兩佐軍用。

translations.literal: One hundred thousand taels of gold and silver from the inner treasury were issued to support military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand taels of gold and silver from the inner treasury were released for the army.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「軍中將士有犯，除連職奏聞，餘依軍法約量決責，有功者依格遷賞。

translations.literal: An edict said: "When officers and soldiers in the army commit offenses, except those involving connected offices which shall be reported to the throne, the rest shall be judged and punished according to military law as appropriate; those with merit shall be promoted and rewarded according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed: "Army offenses, except where the whole chain of command must be reported to the throne, shall be judged and punished under military law. Meritorious service shall be promoted and rewarded by regulation.

sentences.zh: 」以大名尹宗尹為河南路統軍使，河南路統軍都監蒲察世傑為西北路副統，賜弓矢佩刀廄馬，從忠義征行。

translations.literal: " Da Ming Prefect Zong Yin was made Henan Route army commander; Henan Route army deputy overseer Pucha Shijie was made Northwestern Route deputy commander; they were granted bows, arrows, girdled swords, and stable horses, and accompanied Zhongyi on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: " Da Ming Prefect Zong Yin became Henan Route army commander, and Henan Route deputy overseer Pucha Shijie became Northwestern Route deputy commander. Both received bows, arrows, girdled swords, and mounts from the imperial stables and marched with Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 詔諭諸軍將士曰：「兵久駐邊陲，蠹費財用無成功，百姓不得休息。

translations.literal: An edict addressed the various armies' officers and soldiers: "The troops have long encamped on the frontier, wasting resources without success, and the people cannot rest.
translations.idiomatic: The court addressed every officer and soldier: "Your armies have lingered on the frontier for months, draining the treasury without victory while the people know no peace.

sentences.zh: 今命平章政事僕散忠義兼右副元帥，同心戮力以底戡定。

translations.literal: Now Grand Councilor Pusan Zhongyi is appointed concurrently Right Deputy Grand Marshal; with united hearts and combined strength let the campaign be brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Pusan Zhongyi is now Right Deputy Grand Marshal. With one heart and one will, bring this war to its end.

sentences.zh: 右副元帥謀衍罷為同判大宗正事。」

translations.literal: Right Deputy Grand Marshal Moyan Yan was dismissed and made Associate Director of the Imperial Clan Office."
translations.idiomatic: Right Deputy Grand Marshal Moyan Yan was relieved and appointed Associate Director of the Imperial Clan Office."

sentences.zh: 詔居庸關、古北口譏察契丹奸細，捕獲者加官賞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered inspection and surveillance at Juyong Pass and Gubeikou for Khitan spies; those captured would receive promotions and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered heightened scrutiny at Juyong Pass and Gubeikou for Khitan spies, with promotions and rewards for those captured.

sentences.zh: 萬戶溫蒂罕阿魯帶以兵四千屯古北口，薊州、石門關等處各以五百人守之。

translations.literal: Chiliarch Wendihan Arudai encamped at Gubeikou with four thousand troops; Jizhou, Shimen Pass, and other places were each garrisoned with five hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Chiliarch Wendihan Arudai took four thousand men to Gubeikou. Jizhou, Shimen Pass, and other posts each received five-hundred-man garrisons.

sentences.zh: 海陵末年，阿魯帶為猛安，移剌娜為牌印祗候，起契丹部族兵被執，至是挺身來降。

translations.literal: In the closing years of the Hailing reign Arudai was a meng'an and Yila Na was a seal-and-document attendant; when Khitan tribal levies were conscripted they were seized, and now at length they broke free and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of the Hailing reign Arudai had been a meng'an and Yila Na a seal attendant. Both had been seized when Khitan tribal levies were conscripted. Now they escaped and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 世宗以阿魯帶為濟州押軍萬戶，移剌娜為同知濼州事。

translations.literal: Shizong made Arudai Ji Prefecture Escort Army chiliarch and Yila Na associate prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong appointed Arudai Escort Army chiliarch of Ji Prefecture and Yila Na associate prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 西南路招討使完顏思敬為都統，賜金牌一、銀牌二，西北路招討使唐括孛古底副之。

translations.literal: Southwest Route Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Sijing was made commander-in-chief and granted one gold plate and two silver plates; Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Tanggu Bogede served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest Route Pacification Commissioner Wanyan Sijing became overall commander, granted one gold tally and two silver tallies, with Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Tanggu Bogede as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 以兵五千往會燕子城舊戍軍，視地形沖要或於狗濼屯駐，遠斥候，賊至即戰，不以晝夜為限。

translations.literal: With five thousand troops he was to join the old garrison at Swallow City, and depending on terrain where critical, perhaps encamp at Gou Marsh; set distant scouts; when rebels arrived, fight at once without regard to day or night.
translations.idiomatic: With five thousand men he was to unite with the garrison at Swallow City and encamp wherever the terrain demanded, perhaps at Gou Marsh. Long-range scouts were to be posted; when rebels appeared the army was to engage without pause, day or night.

sentences.zh: 詔思敬曰：「契丹賊敗必走山后，可選新馬三千，加芻纇以備追襲。」

translations.literal: An edict told Sijing: "When the Khitan rebels are defeated they will surely flee beyond the mountains; select three thousand fresh horses and add fodder to prepare for pursuit."
translations.idiomatic: Sijing was instructed: "Defeated Khitan rebels will flee into the northern hills. Prepare three thousand fresh horses with ample fodder for the pursuit."

sentences.zh: 僕散忠義至軍中。

translations.literal: Pusan Zhongyi arrived at the army.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Zhongyi reached the front.

sentences.zh: 是時，窩斡西走花道，眾尚八萬。

translations.literal: At that time Wo Wo was fleeing west along Huadao, and his force still numbered eighty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo was then fleeing west along Huadao with a force still eighty thousand strong.

sentences.zh: 忠義、高忠建軍與賊遇，萬戶查剌、蒲查為左翼，宗亨統之；

translations.literal: The armies of Zhongyi and Gao Zhongjian encountered the rebels; chiliarchs Zhala and Pucha formed the left wing under Zong Heng's command;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi and Gao Zhongjian's armies met the rebels. Chiliarchs Zhala and Pucha led the left wing under Zong Heng;

sentences.zh: 宗寧、剌撒為右翼，宗敘統之；

translations.literal: Zong Ning and Lasa formed the right wing under Zong Xu's command;
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ning and Lasa led the right wing under Zong Xu;

sentences.zh: 世傑亦在左翼中，與賊夾河為陣。

translations.literal: Shijie was also in the left wing; the two sides faced each other across a river in battle formation.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie fought in the left wing as the armies formed on opposite banks of a river.

sentences.zh: 賊渡河，以兵四萬餘先犯左翼軍，查剌以六百騎奮擊敗之。

translations.literal: The rebels crossed the river; more than forty thousand troops first struck the left wing, and Zhala with six hundred horsemen charged fiercely and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels crossed the river and hit the left wing first with more than forty thousand men. Zhala led six hundred horsemen in a fierce charge and broke them.

sentences.zh: 複以四萬眾與左翼軍戰，宗亨、世傑七謀克指畫失宜，陣亂敗於賊。

translations.literal: Again with forty thousand they fought the left wing; the seven company commanders under Zong Heng and Shijie directed affairs unsuitably, the formation fell into disorder, and they were defeated by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels returned with forty thousand men. Zong Heng's and Shijie's seven company commanders misdirected the battle, the line collapsed, and the left wing was routed.

sentences.zh: 世傑挺身投于查剌軍中，賊圍查剌軍，查剌力戰，宗敘以右翼軍來救，賊乃去。

translations.literal: Shijie threw himself into Zhala's army; the rebels surrounded Zhala's force; Zhala fought fiercely; Zong Xu came with the right wing to rescue, and the rebels then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie threw himself in with Zhala's detachment. The rebels encircled Zhala, who fought on grimly until Zong Xu brought the right wing to the rescue and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「自契丹作逆，有為賊詿誤者，不問如何從賊，但能複業，與免本罪。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Since the Khitan rose in rebellion, those misled into joining the rebels — regardless of how they followed the rebels — if they can return to their occupations, their original crimes shall be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Since the Khitan rebellion began, all who were misled into joining the rebels — no matter how they came to serve them — shall be pardoned if they return to honest livelihood.

sentences.zh: 如能率眾來附，或能殺捕首領而降，或執送賊所扇誘作亂之人，皆與量加官爵。

translations.literal: If they can lead multitudes to attach themselves, or kill and capture leaders and surrender, or seize and deliver persons the rebels incited to rebellion, all shall receive appropriate additional ranks and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Those who bring followers in surrender, kill or capture rebel leaders, or deliver those the rebels incited to revolt shall be promoted and ennobled according to merit.

sentences.zh: 朕念正隆南征，猛安亡者招還被戮，已命其子孫襲其職。

translations.literal: I recall that during the Zhenglong southern campaign, meng'an who had fled and been recalled were executed; I have already ordered their sons and grandsons to inherit their offices.
translations.idiomatic: I remember the Zhenglong southern campaign, when recalled deserter meng'an were executed. I have already ordered their sons and grandsons to inherit those offices.

sentences.zh: 爾等勿懲前事，故懷遲疑。

translations.literal: You must not take warning from those earlier events and therefore harbor hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let those past punishments make you hesitate now.

sentences.zh: 賊軍今既破散，山后諸處皆命將士遏其逃路，爾等雖欲不降終將安往？

translations.literal: The rebel army is now broken and scattered; everywhere beyond the mountains orders have gone out for officers and soldiers to block their escape routes — even if you wish not to surrender, where in the end can you go?
translations.idiomatic: The rebel army is shattered. Every pass beyond the mountains is blocked. Even if you refuse to submit, where can you go?

sentences.zh: 若猶疑貳，俱就焚滅，悔及矣。」

translations.literal: If you still waver in double-mindedness, you will all be burned and destroyed — it will be too late for regret."
translations.idiomatic: If you still hold back, you will all be destroyed together — and then it will be too late for regret."

sentences.zh: 窩斡自花道西走，僕散忠義、紇石烈志甯以大軍追及於嫋嶺西陷泉。

translations.literal: Wo Wo fled west from Huadao; Pusan Zhongyi and Heishilie Zhining with the main army overtook him west of Niao Ridge at Xian Spring.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo fled west from Huadao. Pusan Zhongyi and Heishilie Zhining overtook him with the main army west of Niao Ridge at Xian Spring.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊軍三萬騎涉水而東。

translations.literal: The next day thirty thousand rebel horsemen waded the water and moved east.
translations.idiomatic: The next day thirty thousand rebel horsemen forded eastward.

sentences.zh: 大軍先據南岡，左翼軍自岡為陣，迤邐而北，步軍繼之，右翼軍繼步軍北引而東，作偃月陣，步軍居中，騎兵據其兩端，使賊不見首尾。

translations.literal: The great army first seized the southern ridge; the left wing formed ranks from the ridge, winding northward, with infantry following; the right wing followed the infantry north and then east, forming a crescent array with infantry in the center and cavalry at both ends so the rebels could not see head or tail.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army seized the southern ridge first. The left wing formed along it and wound north, infantry following. The right wing trailed the infantry north and then east in a crescent formation — infantry in the center, cavalry at both horns — so the rebels could see neither head nor tail.

sentences.zh: 是日，大霧晦冥，既陣霧開，少頃晴霽，賊見左翼據南岡不敢擊，擊右翼軍，烏延查剌力戰，賊稍卻。

translations.literal: That day thick fog obscured everything; once ranks were formed the fog lifted, and shortly afterward skies cleared; the rebels saw the left wing holding the southern ridge and did not dare attack; they attacked the right wing; Wuyan Zhala fought fiercely and the rebels fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: That day fog hung thick. As the armies formed it lifted, and soon the sky cleared. Seeing the left wing hold the southern ridge, the rebels struck the right instead. Wuyan Zhala fought hard and drove them back slightly.

sentences.zh: 志甯與夾穀清臣、烏林答剌撒、鐸剌合戰，賊大敗，將涉水去，泥濘不得亟渡。

translations.literal: Zhining together with Jiagu Qingchen, Ulin Da Lasa, and Dela joined battle; the rebels were utterly defeated and were about to cross the water, but the mud was too deep to cross quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining, Jiagu Qingchen, Ulin Da Lasa, and Dela closed in. The rebels were routed as they tried to ford the river, but the mud held them fast.

sentences.zh: 大軍逐北，人馬相蹂踐而死，不可勝數，陷泉皆平，餘眾蹈籍而過，或奔潰竄匿林莽間。

translations.literal: The great army pursued north; men and horses trampled one another to death beyond counting; Xian Spring was leveled level; the remaining multitude crossed by treading over the dead, while some fled in rout and hid in thickets.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army pressed the pursuit. Men and horses trampled each other to death beyond count until Xian Spring ran level with the ground. Survivors crossed on the fallen bodies; others fled into the brush.

sentences.zh: 大軍踵擊之，俘斬萬計，生擒其弟偽六院司大王嫋。

translations.literal: The great army followed and struck them; captives and kills numbered in the tens of thousands; his younger brother, the false Six-Yuan-Division Prince Niao, was taken alive.
translations.idiomatic: The army hunted them down, taking tens of thousands killed or captured alive, including Wo Wo's younger brother, the pretender Prince Niao of the Six Yuan Offices.

sentences.zh: 窩斡僅與數騎脫去，鈔兀、清臣追四十餘裏不及，斬千餘級，獲車帳甚眾。

translations.literal: Wo Wo escaped with only a few horsemen; Chaowu and Qingchen pursued more than forty li without overtaking them, beheading more than a thousand and capturing a great many carts and tents.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo escaped with only a handful of riders. Chaowu and Qingchen pursued forty li without catching him, taking more than a thousand heads and vast numbers of carts and tents.

sentences.zh: 其母徐輦舉營自落括岡西走，志寧追之，盡獲輜重，俘五萬餘人，雜畜不可勝計。

translations.literal: His mother Xulian raised camp and fled west from Luoguo Ridge; Zhining pursued, capturing all baggage completely, taking more than fifty thousand prisoners, and livestock beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo's mother Xulian broke camp and fled west from Luoguo Ridge. Zhining overtook her, seizing all her baggage, more than fifty thousand captives, and livestock beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 偽節度使六及其部族皆降。

translations.literal: The false military commissioner Liu and his tribe all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The pretender military commissioner Liu and his clansmen surrendered en masse.

sentences.zh: 詔北京副統完顏達吉括本部馬，規辦芻糧，仍使達吉為監戰官，錄有功者聞奏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Northern Capital deputy commander Wanyan Daji to muster his command's horses and arrange fodder and grain; Daji was also made battle overseer to record the meritorious and report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Capital deputy commander Wanyan Daji was ordered to gather his command's horses and procure fodder. He was also made battle overseer to record merit and report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔選中都、西京兩路新舊軍萬人備守禦，以窩斡敗走，恐或衝突也。

translations.literal: An edict ordered selection of ten thousand troops old and new from the Central Capital and Western Capital routes for defense, because Wo Wo had been defeated and fled and might break through in a raid.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand troops from the Central Capital and Western Capital routes were mobilized for defense, lest the fleeing Wo Wo break through somewhere.

sentences.zh: 僕散忠義使使奏捷，詔略曰：「平章政事右副元帥忠義使使來奏大捷。

translations.literal: Pusan Zhongyi sent envoys to report victory; the edict in summary said: "Grand Councilor and Right Deputy Grand Marshal Zhongyi's envoys come reporting a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Zhongyi sent messengers bearing news of victory. The edict read in part: "Grand Councilor and Right Deputy Grand Marshal Zhongyi's envoys report a great victory.

sentences.zh: 或被軍俘獲，或自能來服，或無所歸而投拜，或將全屬歸附，或分領家族來降，或嘗受偽命，及自來曾與官軍鬥敵，皆釋其罪。

translations.literal: Whether captured by the army, or coming to submit of their own ability, or having nowhere to turn and bowing in allegiance, or bringing entire dependents to attach themselves, or leading families in separate groups to surrender, or having once received false appointments, or having formerly fought against the government army — all shall have their crimes released.
translations.idiomatic: Whether taken in battle, coming forward to submit, bowing allegiance with nowhere else to turn, bringing whole households, leading clansmen in surrender, having served under the pretender, or having fought imperial troops — all shall be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 其散亡人內，除窩斡一身，不以大小官員是何名色，卻來歸附者，亦准釋放。

translations.literal: Among those scattered and lost, aside from Wo Wo alone, regardless of what rank or title high or low they held, those who return to attach themselves shall likewise be released from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Among the scattered remnant, apart from Wo Wo himself, all who return to submit — whatever rank or title they once held — shall likewise be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 有能誅捕窩斡，或於不從招納亡去人內誅捕以來，及或能率眾于掌軍官及隨處官司投降者，並給官賞。

translations.literal: Those who can kill or capture Wo Wo, or among those who fled refusing summons kill or capture and bring them in, or those who can lead multitudes to surrender to army commanders or local offices — all shall be granted official rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever kills or captures Wo Wo, or delivers those who fled after refusing surrender, or leads groups to surrender to local commanders or officials shall receive official reward.

sentences.zh: 各路撫納來者，毋得輒加侵損。

translations.literal: On every route those who receive and settle newcomers must not rashly add harm or injury.
translations.idiomatic: Every command that receives surrendering rebels must not molest or plunder them.

sentences.zh: 無資給者，不以是何路分，隨有糧處安置，仍官為養濟。」

translations.literal: Those without provisions, regardless of what route they belong to, shall be settled wherever grain is available, and still be nourished and supported by the state."
translations.idiomatic: Those without means shall be settled wherever grain is available, regardless of route, and maintained at public expense."

sentences.zh: 窩斡收合散卒萬餘人，遂入奚部，以諸奚自益，時時出兵寇速魯古澱、古北口、興化之間。

translations.literal: Wo Wo gathered scattered soldiers into more than ten thousand, then entered Xi territory, augmenting himself with various Xi people, and from time to time sent troops to raid between Sulugu Marsh, Gubeikou, and Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Wo regrouped more than ten thousand scattered troops and entered Xi territory, recruiting Xi warriors to his cause. He raided repeatedly between Sulugu Marsh, Gubeikou, and Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 溫蒂罕阿魯帶守古北口，與戰敗焉。

translations.literal: Wendihan Arudai guarded Gubeikou and was defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wendihan Arudai held Gubeikou and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 詔完顏謀衍、蒲察烏裏雅、蒲察蒲盧渾以兵三千，合舊屯兵五千，擊之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wanyan Moyan Yan, Pucha Wuliya, and Pucha Puluhun with three thousand troops, joining the five thousand already encamped, to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Moyan Yan, Pucha Wuliya, and Pucha Puluhun were ordered to take three thousand men, combined with five thousand already in garrison, to attack him.

sentences.zh: 詔守顏思敬以所部兵入奚地，會大軍討窩斡。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Wanyan Sijing to enter Xi territory with his troops and join the great army in suppressing Wo Wo.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Sijing was ordered to march his command into Xi territory and join the main army against Wo Wo.

sentences.zh: 賊黨霿𩃭河猛安蒲速越遣人至帥府約降，詔令擒捕窩斡，許以官賞。

translations.literal: Rebel partisan Menglong River meng'an Pusuyue sent men to the command headquarters to arrange surrender; an edict ordered Wo Wo seized and captured, promising official reward.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel meng'an Pusuyue of the Menglong River sent emissaries to the headquarters offering surrender. The court promised official reward for capturing Wo Wo.

sentences.zh: 賊將降者甚眾。

translations.literal: Rebel generals surrendering were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel officers surrendered in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 其散走者聞詔書招降，亦多降者。

translations.literal: Those scattered in flight who heard the edict summoning surrender also surrendered in large numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Stragglers who heard the surrender proclamation also came in in droves.

sentences.zh: 其餘多疾疫而死，無複鬥志。

translations.literal: The rest mostly died of pestilence and no longer had will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder mostly died of plague and lost all will to fight.

sentences.zh: 窩斡自度勢窮，乃謀自羊城道西京奔夏國，大軍追之益急，其眾複多亡去，度不得西，乃北走沙陀間。

translations.literal: Wo Wo judged his situation desperate; he then planned to flee to Western Xia by way of Sheep City Road and the Western Capital; the great army pursued ever more urgently; his multitude again deserted in large numbers; judging he could not go west, he then fled north into the Shatuo region.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his cause hopeless, Wo Wo planned to flee west through Sheep City Road and the Western Capital into Xia territory. Pursuit tightened and more men deserted. Unable to break west, he turned north into the Shatuo country.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書省：「凡脅從之家被俘掠遂致離散，宜從改正。

translations.literal: An edict to the Ministry of Works: "All families of the coerced who were captured and plundered and thereby scattered should have their registers corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Works was instructed: "Families of those forced into rebellion, scattered by capture and plunder, shall have their household registers corrected.

sentences.zh: 將士往往藏匿其人，有司檢括分付。」

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers often hide such persons; the authorities shall search and assign them back."
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers have often hidden such people. The authorities shall search them out and restore them to their families."

sentences.zh: 監軍志寧獲賊稍合住，釋而弗殺，縱還賊中，使誘其親近捕窩斡以自效，許以官賞。

translations.literal: Overseer Zhining captured the rebel Shaoxinghe, released him without killing him, and sent him back into the rebel camp to induce his intimates to capture Wo Wo as merit in his place, promising official reward.
translations.idiomatic: Overseer Zhining captured the rebel Shaoxinghe, spared his life, and sent him back among the rebels to persuade his confederates to capture Wo Wo in exchange for reward.

sentences.zh: 九月庚子，稍合住與神獨斡執窩斡，詣右都臨完顏思敬降，並獲其母徐輦及其妻、子、子婦、弟、侄，盡收偽金銀牌印。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the ninth month, Shaoxinghe and Shenduwo seized Wo Wo and went to Right Deputy Overseer Wanyan Sijing to surrender, also capturing his mother Xulian and his wife, sons, daughters-in-law, younger brother, and nephews, and gathering all false gold and silver tally-seals.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day of the ninth month Shaoxinghe and Shenduwo seized Wo Wo and surrendered to Right Deputy Overseer Wanyan Sijing. They also took his mother Xulian, wife, sons, daughters-in-law, brother, and nephews, and collected all the rebel gold and silver tallies.

sentences.zh: 唐括孛古底獲前胡裏改節度使什溫及其家屬。

translations.literal: Tanggu Bogede captured former Huligai Military Commissioner Shiwen and his family members.
translations.idiomatic: Tanggu Bogede captured former Huligai Military Commissioner Shiwen and his household.

sentences.zh: 西北路招討使李家奴獲偽樞密使逐斡等三十餘人，複與猛安泥本婆果追偽監軍那也至天成縣，那也乃降，乃獲偽都元帥醜哥及金牌一、銀牌五。

translations.literal: Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Li Jianu captured the false Privy Councilor Zhuwo and more than thirty others; again with meng'an Niben Boguo he pursued false overseer Naye to Tiancheng County; Naye then surrendered, and they also captured the false Grand Marshal Chuge and one gold plate and five silver plates.
translations.idiomatic: Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Li Jianu captured the pretender Privy Councilor Zhuwo and more than thirty others. With meng'an Niben Boguo he pursued pretender overseer Naye to Tiancheng County. Naye surrendered, and they also took pretender Grand Marshal Chuge along with one gold tally and five silver tallies.

sentences.zh: 志甯與清臣、宗甯、速哥等追餘黨至燕子城，盡得其黨。

translations.literal: Zhining with Qingchen, Zong Ning, Suge, and others pursued remaining partisans to Swallow City and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining, Qingchen, Zong Ning, Suge, and others hunted the remnant to Swallow City and captured them every one.

sentences.zh: 前至抹拔裏達之地，悉獲之，逆党遂平。

translations.literal: Advancing to Mabali Dada territory, they captured them completely, and the rebel party was thus pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on to Mabali Dada and took all who remained. The rebellion was fully suppressed.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，皇太子率百官上表賀。

translations.literal: On jiachen day the crown prince led the hundred officials in submitting a congratulatory memorial.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day the crown prince led the court in a memorial of congratulation.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，詔天下。

translations.literal: On yisi day an edict was issued to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day the victory was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，完顏思敬獻俘于京師，窩斡梟首於市，磔其手足，分懸諸京府。

translations.literal: On xinhai day Wanyan Sijing presented captives at the capital; Wo Wo's head was displayed in the marketplace, his limbs dismembered, and portions hung in various capitals and prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day Wanyan Sijing presented the captives at court. Wo Wo's head was exposed in the marketplace, his limbs quartered and displayed in capitals across the realm.

sentences.zh: 其母徐輦及妻子皆戮之。

translations.literal: His mother Xulian and wife and children were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Xulian, his wife, and his children were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 契丹降人皆拘其器仗，貧不能自給者官為養濟。

translations.literal: Khitan who surrendered were all required to surrender their weapons; those too poor to support themselves were nourished and maintained by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered Khitan were disarmed. Those too poor to live on their own were maintained at public expense.

sentences.zh: 括裏、紮八率眾南走，詔左宣徽使宗亨追及之。

translations.literal: Kuoli and Zhahe led their multitudes fleeing south; an edict ordered Left Palace Commissioner Zong Heng to pursue and overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: Kuoli and Zhahe fled south with their followers. Left Palace Commissioner Zong Heng was ordered to overtake them.

sentences.zh: 紮八詐稱降，宗亨信其言，遂不與戰。

translations.literal: Zhahe falsely claimed to surrender; Zong Heng believed his words and therefore did not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhahe feigned surrender. Zong Heng believed him and held his army back.

sentences.zh: 紮八紿之曰：「括裏驚走，願追之。

translations.literal: Zhahe deceived him, saying: "Kuoli fled in alarm; I wish to pursue him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhahe tricked him, saying, "Kuoli has fled in panic. Allow me to pursue him.

sentences.zh: 」宗亨縱紮八去。

translations.literal: " Zong Heng released Zhahe to go.
translations.idiomatic: " Zong Heng let Zhahe go.

sentences.zh: 益都猛安欲以所部追括裏、紮八，宗亨恐分其功，不聽，而縱軍士取賊所棄資囊人畜而自有之。

translations.literal: Yidu meng'an wished to pursue Kuoli and Zhahe with his command; Zong Heng feared sharing the credit and would not permit it, but instead allowed soldiers to take the rebels' abandoned goods, bags, livestock, and keep them for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Yidu meng'an asked to pursue Kuoli and Zhahe with his command. Zong Heng, fearing a rival for credit, refused — and instead let his soldiers help themselves to the rebels' abandoned loot and livestock.

sentences.zh: 括裏、紮入由是得亡去，遂奔于宋。

translations.literal: Kuoli and Zhahe thereby were able to escape and flee, and then fled to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Kuoli and Zhahe thus escaped and fled to Song.

sentences.zh: 宗亨降甯州剌史。

translations.literal: Zong Heng was demoted to Prefect of Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Heng was demoted to prefect of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 其後，宋李世輔用括裏、紮八，遂取宿州，頗為邊患。

translations.literal: Later, Song's Li Shipu employed Kuoli and Zhahe, then took Suzhou, and they became quite a frontier menace.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Song general Li Shipu employed Kuoli and Zhahe to seize Suzhou, and they became a lasting frontier threat.

sentences.zh: 神獨斡除同知安化軍節度使，稍合住除同知震武軍節度使事。

translations.literal: Shenduwo was made Associate Military Commissioner of Anhua Army; Shaoxinghe was made Associate Military Commissioner of Zhenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shenduwo was appointed associate military commissioner of Anhua Army and Shaoxinghe associate military commissioner of Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 大定六年，點檢司奏，親軍中有逆黨子弟，請一切罷去。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dading, the Palace Inspectorate memorialized that among the personal guard were sons and younger brothers of rebel partisans and requested that all be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading year six the Palace Inspectorate reported that sons and brothers of rebel families served in the imperial guard and requested their dismissal.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「身預逆黨者罷之，餘勿問。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Those who personally joined the rebel party shall be dismissed; the rest need not be investigated."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Dismiss only those who joined the rebellion themselves. Leave the rest alone."

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金人以燕山與宋，遂啟張覺跳樑之心，覺豈為宋者哉，蓋欲乘時以徼利耳。

translations.literal: The encomium says: When the Jin people ceded Yanshan to Song, they thereby aroused Zhang Jue's ambition to vault the beam; did Jue act for Song? He merely wished to seize the moment and wrest profit.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Ceding Yanshan to Song planted in Zhang Jue the ambition of the beam-vaulter. Jue was no servant of Song — he sought only to grab profit while fortune smiled.

sentences.zh: 耶律余睹從宗望追天祚，曾不遺餘力，功成驕溢，自取誅滅，咈哉。

translations.literal: Ye Lü Yudu followed Zongwang in pursuing Emperor Tianzuo, sparing no effort whatsoever; when merit was achieved pride overflowed and he brought execution upon himself — alas.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Lü Yudu followed Zongwang in hunting down Emperor Tianzuo and held nothing back. Success bred arrogance and brought him to the execution ground. Pitiful.

sentences.zh: 正隆佳兵，契丹作難，《傳》曰：「夫兵猶火也，弗戢將自焚。

translations.literal: In the Zhenglong reign he honored weapons; the Khitan rose in difficulty; the Commentary says: "Warfare is like fire; if not restrained it will burn oneself.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhenglong reign glorified war, and the Khitan rose in revolt. The Commentary says: "War is like fire; unchecked, it consumes its master.

sentences.zh: 」可不戒哉！

translations.literal: " How can one not be warned!
translations.idiomatic: " Let this be a warning!
